data.title: Bus Bunching
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“公交车扎堆”现象：当两辆或多辆公交车按相同路线和间隔发车时，若某辆车因交通拥堵延误，它会因载上更多乘客而进一步落后于 schedule。与此同时，后面的车由于乘客较少，行进更快，最终可能赶上甚至超过前面的车，导致它们扎堆到站。解决办法包括设置每站的停留时间限制、允许某些站点不停靠、鼓励乘客等候较空的车，以及像北亚利桑那大学那样，放弃固定时刻表，通过延时来保持车辆间距。简单增加车辆并不能解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公交车调度与拥挤问题的解决方案

不同观点：
• **支持灵活调度与动态管理**：  
  - sebstefan认为可以通过设定每个站点的最短和最长停留时间，甚至在高峰期跳过某些站点来缓解拥挤，并举例北亚利桑那大学通过放弃固定时刻表来保持车辆均匀间隔。
  - nix0n支持跳过某些站点，因为在波士顿地区，后面的公交车超过前面的车能减少乘客集中在同一辆车上，从而缓解拥挤问题。

• **质疑灵活调度的可靠性**：  
  - lexlambda反对跳过站点，认为这会破坏公交系统的可靠性，尤其对需要换乘的乘客造成不便。无时刻表也会导致换乘问题。
  - anonymous_sorry提到在伦敦地铁或公交车上，人为延迟车辆以平衡服务间隔会引起乘客不满，但从系统角度看可能有其合理性。

• **技术解决方案**：  
  - AndrewDucker建议在站点设置数字公交时刻表，让乘客实时了解公交运行情况，从而做出明智选择。
  - plantwallshoe分享了西雅图的实时公交追踪应用如何改善其乘车体验，使乘客无需依赖固定时刻表。

• **基础设施改进建议**：  
  - this15testingg和Lvl999Noob强调公交专用车道的重要性，认为不应让私人汽车延误公共交通。Lvl999Noob还提出需要足够频密的服务、高峰期运力、教育宣传和外部干预（如罚款）等综合措施。

补充讨论：
• **具体案例与经验分享**：  
  - dmd提到25年前曾描述过类似的公交系统问题。
  - kevin_thibedeau抱怨纽约地铁的调度问题，特别是当快车因等待慢车而延迟时。
  - dang提供了多个相关讨论链接，包括关于公交车拥挤问题的历史讨论。

争议焦点：
• **跳站与无时刻表调度的可行性与可靠性**：一部分人认为这些措施能有效缓解拥挤，但另一部分人担心这会降低系统的整体可靠性，并对乘客造成不便。

44625493.article_content:
Bus Bunching
Image:
Wikimedia Commons
When two or more buses are scheduled at regular intervals on the same route, planners may expect that each will make the same progress, pausing at each stop for the same interval (1). But if Bus B is delayed by traffic congestion (2), it incurs a penalty: Because it arrives late to the next stop, it will pick up some passengers who’d planned to take Bus C (3). Accommodating these passengers delays Bus B even longer, putting it even further behind schedule. Meanwhile, Bus C begins to make unusually good progress (4), as it now arrives at each stop to find a smaller crowd than expected.
As the workload piles up on the foremost bus and the one behind it catches up, eventually the result (5) is that the two buses run in a platoon, arriving together at each stop. Sometimes Bus C even overtakes Bus B.
What to do? Planners can set minimum and maximum amounts of time to be spent at each stop, and buses might even be told to skip certain stops during crowded runs. Passengers might be encouraged to wait for a following bus, with the inducement that it’s less crowded. Northern Arizona University improved its service by abandoning the idea of a schedule altogether and delaying buses at certain stops in order to maintain even spacing. One thing that doesn’t work: adding vehicles to the route — which might, at first blush, have seemed the obvious solution.
July 12, 2025
|
Science & Math

data.title: Solving a Childhood Mystery: How BASIC Games Learned to Win
data.author: greentec
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讲述了作者回顾自己年少时使用BASIC语言编写游戏的经历，特别是重新审视一本旧的BASIC编程书籍。书中包含一个名为Hexapawn的小型国际象棋变种游戏的源码，该游戏在一个较小的棋盘上进行，目标是消灭对手的棋子或到达对方底线。

文章详细解释了BASIC语言中**DATA**命令的作用，它用于预存储常量值，并通过**READ**命令在程序运行时读取。作者回忆起年少时对这些代码的困惑，特别是源码中出现的大量数字。通过向AI助手Claude.ai请教，作者终于理解了这些数字的含义。

文章还提供了Hexapawn游戏的JavaScript版本链接和源码，并解释了BASIC编程中的行号及其重要性。总的来说，这篇文章通过作者的个人经历，介绍了BASIC编程语言的一些基本概念和历史背景。

主要讨论点：David Ahl将作品公有领域化及其相关资源，以及对Hexapawn和机器学习算法的讨论。

不同观点：
• [kragen] David Ahl已将其所有作品纳入公有领域，包括一本书，并且提供了原书的Hexapawn页面链接。然而，kragen不知道是否有韩文版的在线资源。

• [JLemay] 提出1970年代是许多基础机器学习算法和概念诞生的时期，并提到决策树算法、聚类和集成方法等研究。他还指出第一个决策树算法在1973年创建，强调了早期研究的时间点。

• [louthy] 回忆过去从杂志和书中输入代码列表的经历，提到一个字符错误会导致整个程序失败，而当时并没有足够的知识去修复。

• [diggernet] 讨论了代码中第511行的问题，指出它实际上是以"511 REM"开头，并且在REM后不需要跟空格。

• [jerf] 分享了Matt Parker的一个视频链接，视频内容是关于MENACE的物理实现，作为博物馆展示的一部分。

• [reverendsteveii] 表示想重写高中时期编写的无败的井字棋算法，希望算法从潜在的游戏状态中逐步消除失败的走法，而不是一开始就优化。

• [michalpleban] 质疑为何不直接使用一个较小的走法表，从一开始就去掉失败的走法，而非要从失败中学习。

• [Mountain_Skies] 提到在《The Rainbow》杂志上有一篇关于井字棋珠算法（机器学习）的文章，并认为由于算法和游戏的简单性，使其在记忆中留存较久。

• [jgalt212] 提供了Gardner在《科学美国人》上关于Hexapawn的文章PDF链接。

补充讨论：
• 对Hexapawn及其算法的兴趣和怀旧情感是讨论的一个重要部分。
• 对机器学习早期算法的历史背景和发展的讨论也是一个焦点，尤其是决策树算法的起源。
• 争议焦点在于为何通过失败学习而不是直接使用优化后的走法表，这引发了对算法效率和学习机制的进一步思考。

Background
From my teenage years until now, I’ve kept an old BASIC book. It’s a translated version of “BASIC Computer Games” written by David H. Ahl. BASIC (Beginner’s All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code) is an old programming language designed to be easy for beginners to use. It was probably easier to use than assembler or C. I remember later creating a text-based game where seven countries fought each other in turn-based combat. It was my first game that I was quite proud of, but I’ve since lost the source code.
The reason this is labeled as Volume 1 is that it doesn’t include all the games from
the original
that I recently looked up out of nostalgia. Perhaps the editorial team omitted some games during the translation into my native language. No Yahtzee! However, they seem to have faithfully transcribed the source code without typos. Since someone has uploaded these to
GitHub
, I was saved the trouble of retyping the source code for this review.
Opening this book brought back an old mystery from the depths of my memory. It was the source code for a game called
Hexapawn
. While other programs were difficult enough for me to understand, this one was particularly challenging.
Hexapawn
Let’s first understand what this game is about. It’s a type of
minichess
. Minichess is a chess variant played on a board smaller than the standard 8x8 chessboard, usually with fewer pieces. The game becomes simpler and more concise than regular chess, and is often used for educational purposes or as a proof of concept. I recently created a
minichess
game with three different game modes.
As the name suggests, this game features 6 pawns, with two players each having 3. The goal is to either eliminate all of the opponent’s pieces or reach the end of the board (the opponent’s starting line) before they do.
The complete source code for Hexapawn from BASIC Computer Games can be found
here
. In this blog post, I won’t review the entire code, but will focus on the parts that interest me.

The DATA command appears, followed by a series of meaningless numbers. -1, 0, 1 appear, then suddenly two-digit numbers appear with 0s, and it abruptly ends. It feels like listening to Radiohead’s music after their 4th album, which I still can’t follow. Can you understand the frustration I felt as a child trying to understand this source code?
So what is this source code? And what is
DATA
? When I asked my friend Claude.ai, I got the answer.
First, unlike modern programming languages, BASIC requires you to write line numbers directly for each line, followed by a space before the actual command. Line numbers don’t have to be sequential, but they’re usually arranged in ascending order. This is because readability makes maintenance and reuse more convenient. When I learned it in the old days, I used line numbers in increments of 10 like 10, 20, 30. This was because you might need to insert other line numbers like 15 in between.
For example, a BASIC code that receives a value A and immediately prints it would look like this:
10
INPUT
A
20
PRINT
A
In BASIC syntax,
DATA
is a command that pre-stores constant values to be used during program execution. During execution, these data can be read sequentially through the
READ
command.

data.title: What does connecting with someone mean?
data.author: bradwoodsio
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了人与人之间建立联系的重要性以及其中的困难。联系意味着彼此 empathy（共情）—— 理解对方并被对方理解，发现共同的价值观、经历和视角，从而建立信任和安全感。作者反思自己人生中最幸福的时刻，发现大部分都与人际连接有关，因此创办了一个网站来促进这种联系。然而，随着成长，人们因害怕受伤而筑起心理防线，导致难以真正与他人连接。文章呼吁通过放下防备、真诚交流来克服孤独，寻求幸福。这需要勇气，但也是建立深层人际关系的关键。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小谈的价值与人际连接的作用

不同观点：
• **wanderingstan** 认为小谈是人际连接的起点，尽管它看似表面，但提供了一个相互认可和探索共同价值观的机会。小谈是建立关系的初始阶段，深度交流会随着时间自然发展。
• **JLemay** 强调同理心在加强人际连接中的重要性，并指出社交媒体和个人主义的兴起削弱了这种能力。匿名性和即时满足的心理使得网络上的残酷行为变得常见。
• **2color** 提供了一个避免传统小谈陷阱的实际方法，建议用“你睡得怎么样？”来替代“你好吗？”这种常规问法。
• **nntwozz** 质疑当双方没有相似价值观时该如何处理，引用了林肯的名言来表达对理解不同观点的必要性。
• **bovermyer** 提出了关于何时该展现脆弱感与过度分享之间界限的疑问。
• **Notatheist** 反驳了小谈阻碍连接的观点，认为连接可以在没有交换有价值信息的情况下发生，小谈实际上是衡量一个人连接能力的标准。
• **inezk** 比较了美国和波兰的问候文化，指出浅层的问候在不同文化中可能有不同的作用，同时提到欧洲更好的工作生活平衡有助于建立人际关系。
• **cloverich** 分享了个人经验，强调小谈之后自然发展出的深层次连接，但也指出一开始就“点击”的连接感同样重要，不应强求小谈。
• **satisfice** 指出并非所有人都讨厌小谈，有些人只是不舒适或不愿意让小谈引导到深层次话题。他们可能对小谈的处理方式感到不安，而不是真正讨厌它。

• **codeful** 简单评论了文章的质量和启发性。
• **micromacrofoot** 提供了一个与主话题无关的技术建议。

• 小谈是否真的阻碍了深度人际连接，还是它是建立关系的必要起点。

• 不同文化背景对小谈及其作用的不同看法。

44669368.article_content:
Published on 24th July 2025
Connect
I read a lot about the idea of connecting with people. They
say it's the reason to get good at conversation — so you can
connect. A problem I had with this advice is I couldn't find
a good explanation of what connecting means.
It means mutual empathy — they
get
you and you
get
them. It's discovering similar values,
experiences and perspectives. It's a feeling of trust
and comfort where you both feel safe to say what is
truly on your mind.
That feeling is why I started this website. Six months I
asked myself what should I do for the rest of my life. A
good place to start was to figure out what makes me happy.
So, I wrote down the best experiences of my life so far. I
came up with 20. 19 of them were experiences where I
connected with people.
Humans need connection. If loneliness is a disease then
connection is the cure. It fills a hole that can't be filled
any other way.
Connecting requires lowering your guard to expose how
you think and feel. This leads to revealing your values,
experiences and perspectives.
People hate small talk because it avoids this. The purpose
of social conversation is to connect but talking about the
weather or the latest sportz ball result reveals sh!t.
Making friends is easy as a kid, hard as an adult
As a child, I didn't have my guard up — because there was
nothing to guard. A six year old hardly has values,
experiences and perspectives. They freely offer how they
think and feel and thus instantly connect with others.
As I grew up, I had experiences where exposing how I thought
and felt resulted in pain. Like when I asked someone out on
a date for the first time and was rejected. That required
exposing deep feelings, making me vulnerable. This mad the
pain of rejection
visceral.
I don't like
pain and try to avoid it. Therefore, I took steps to prevent
that from happening again — by erecting a concrete wall to
prevent anyone seeing who I was interested in. This protects
me. Makes me less vulnerable. As I continued to grow, I had
more of these experiences, so I erected more walls.
By the time we're adults, we have so many walls that trying
to find out what someone thinks or feels is like talking to
a wall. These walls are a double edged sword. They protect
but also isolate. Preventing some painful experiences while
being the source of another — disconnection.
If we want to be happy, we need to have our needs met. This
requires lowering our walls. The next time someone asks
"How are you?"
, try answering honestly.

data.title: PSA: SQLite WAL checksums fail silently and may lose data
data.author: avinassh
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了SQLite数据库在WAL模式下的校验和（checksum）处理机制。尽管SQLite在WAL模式中引入了校验和，但它不会在检测到校验和错误时抛出错误，而是直接丢弃出错帧及其后的所有帧，即使它们未损坏。这种行为是设计使然，不是bug。SQLite在校验和验证过程中，通过单次扫描WAL文件来检查每个帧的校验和，并在发现第一个无效校验和时停止。如果缺少伴随的`.db-shm`文件或在WAL写入时发生不洁关机，就可能触发此问题，导致数据丢失。作者认为，默认行为不应直接截断WAL文件并丢失数据，而应抛出错误让代码处理，并建议提供选项让用户选择是否忽略损坏数据。SQLite的这种设计可能是为了在嵌入式环境或移动设备上更好地运行，而非像企业级数据库那样处理数据损坏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLite中WAL（Write-Ahead Log）的校验和（checksum）功能的目的及其在数据完整性和防崩溃中的作用。

不同观点：
• **teraflop**：认为WAL中的校验和不是为了检测任意的数据损坏，而是为了检测部分写入（partial writes），例如未完全写入的帧。SQLite的校验和主要用于日志（journal），包括回滚日志和WAL，而不是数据库文件本身。写入数据库文件的操作具有幂等性，因此即使在崩溃后也能通过回滚或重放操作恢复。

• **lxgr**：支持teraflop的观点，并进一步指出SQLite依赖于底层系统来处理数据损坏，而不是在自身引入复杂的校验和机制。SQLite的设计假设数据损坏由底层处理，除非另有声明。引入全面的校验和将增加SQLite的复杂性。

• **nemothekid**：认为SQLite的“静默失败”是正常功能，而不是缺陷。如果WAL不完整，SQLite不应通知应用程序，因为这是预期的行为。如果磁盘上的位翻转导致损坏，不应由SQLite负责处理。

• **kburman**：指出SQLite的WAL功能实际上是一种安全设计，防止数据库损坏，而不是导致损坏。将这种行为视为危险缺陷是一种误解。

• **cwillu**：强调SQLite留下的数据库状态是曾经存在的状态，即使这意味着有些提交的事务可能会丢失。这是数据库在面临部分写入失败时的最佳结果。

• **slashdev**：解释了为何SQLite在检测到校验和失败时会丢弃后续帧，因为跳过损坏帧并应用后续帧会导致数据库损坏。

• **jmull**：认为SQLite的校验和不是为了检测数据损坏，而是为了防止物理写入失败（如断电）导致的数据库损坏。抛出错误在这种场景下并不合理。

• **ryanjshaw**：认为SQLite的设计是合理的，因为即使通知应用程序WAL损坏，应用程序的处理方式与忽略未提交事务的处理方式一致。

• **asveikau**：指出如果数据库文件消失，如.db-shm文件，这不是SQLite的错，而是文件系统的问题。

• **dev_l1x_be**：提出唯一真正的解决方案可能是事务性文件系统，但这涉及到重新设计文件系统的工作方式。

• **dathinab**：提到SQLite有一个官方的校验和VFS shim，但它在页面级别工作，且需要手动运行检查。校验和不用于备份或数据恢复。

• **adzm**：认为SQLite应该提供一种方式将校验和错误通知应用程序，以便应用程序能够处理。

• **westurner**：讨论了在SQLite中使用Merkle哈希来增强一致性和数据完整性的可能性，并提到了一些SQLite扩展和相关技术。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于SQLite的校验和功能是否应扩展以检测任意数据损坏，还是保持现有设计以防止部分写入和崩溃恢复。
• 对WAL校验和功能的正确理解和预期用途存在不同看法，部分评论者认为其设计合理并符合预期，而另一些评论者则希望看到更多错误通知和数据完整性检查功能。
• 提出了一些替代技术（如Merkle哈希）来增强SQLite的数据完整性，但这些技术涉及复杂的实现和权衡。

44671373.article_content:
This is a follow-up post to my
PSA: SQLite does not do checksums
and
PSA: Most databases do not do checksums by default
. In the previous posts I mentioned that SQLite does not do checksums by default, but it has checksums in WAL mode. However, on checksum errors, instead of raising error, it drops all the subsequent frames. Even if they are not corrupt. This is not a bug; it’s intentional.
SQLite WAL
SQLite introduced WAL in 2010. It’s not the default mode, but you’re likely using it if you want higher write throughput. Whenever you make writes, they are first written to the WAL file. Then, during checkpoint operations, the database pages are written from the WAL to the main DB file. Each page in the WAL is called a frame. Each frame has a header, which comprises the frame number, page number, commit marker, and checksums.
The way checksums work in WAL is interesting. They use rolling checksums, meaning the checksum of the n+1 frame is computed with the checksum of the nth frame. In other words, a frame’s checksum depends on the previous frame.
Recovery
If one frame is found to have a checksum mismatch, you can’t be sure that the next frame isn’t corrupted either. What’s interesting is that when a frame is found to have a missing or invalid checksum, SQLite drops that frame and all the subsequent frames. This is
documented
:
Recovery works by doing a single pass over the WAL, from beginning to end. The checksums are verified on each frame of the WAL as it is read. The scan stops at the end of the file or at the first invalid checksum. The mxFrame field is set to the index of the last valid commit frame in WAL.
Earlier I mentioned SQLite does not do checksums by default, so it won’t ever notice if a page is corrupt. So when is WAL checksum verification triggered? A WAL may contain multiple frames for the same page number. To make lookups faster, SQLite maintains an index called the WAL Index. This is the
.db-shm
file you often see. During the building of this index, SQLite checks the checksums.
You can verify this in the code as well. The recovery process happens in
walIndexRecover
, this calls
walDecodeFrame
which has this:
/* A frame is only valid if a checksum of the WAL header,
** all prior frames, the first 16 bytes of this frame-header,
** and the frame-data matches the checksum in the last 8
** bytes of this frame-header.
*/
nativeCksum
=
(pWal
->
hdr.bigEndCksum
==
SQLITE_BIGENDIAN);
walChecksumBytes
(nativeCksum, aFrame,
8
, aCksum, aCksum);
walChecksumBytes
(nativeCksum, aData, pWal
->
szPage, aCksum, aCksum);
if
( aCksum[
0
]
!=
sqlite3Get4byte
(
&
aFrame[
16
])
||
aCksum[
1
]
!=
sqlite3Get4byte
(
&
aFrame[
20
])
){
/* Checksum failed. */
return
0
;
}
To trigger this issue, the following needs to happen:
You have SQLite
.db
and
.db-wal
files, but no accompanying
.db-shm
file. Maybe your friend shared it with you, or you downloaded some data off the internet.
Unclean shutdown during WAL write. The WAL index is updated after a successful write. Maybe after the WAL write, the process crashed, and the index wasn’t updated. On the next start, SQLite rebuilds the index.
During this process, if there’s a checksum mismatch on a frame, that frame and the rest of the WAL frames are dropped. Even if they are not corrupt (technically)! Note that SQLite always checkpoints and truncates the WAL file on the last connection close.
Demo
Alice would have lost money,
again
. Poor Alice.
Thoughts
I really don’t like that SQLite doesn’t throw any error on detection of corruption
Since it automatically checkpoints every time, the data is lost too
I’m not sure why this is the default behavior. Backward compatibility reasons? The checksums in WAL are likely not meant to check for random page corruption in the middle; maybe they’re just to check if the last write of a frame was fsynced properly or not?
What I want: throw an error when corruption is detected and let the code handle it. Don’t checkpoint and truncate the WAL! Maybe provide an option for users to opt in to ignore the corruption and work with the existing behavior.
In the demo, I corrupted a frame that belonged to an older version of a page. Meaning no new transactions can ever read that data. That frame is practically useless, yet it caused data loss. There are pages like belonging to an index or maybe some table that we don’t care about at all. With sophisticated recovery mechanisms, we could sometimes able to recover all the data.
Overall, I don’t like this as a default. However,
Pekka Enberg
offered a different perspective that SQLite runs in embedded environments where there’s no server, and maybe core developers decided it may be better to limp along than crash.
I would guess that other databases behave the same way, but I haven’t verified it myself. I was discussing this with
Alex Miller
, and he raised an interesting point: SQLite mostly runs on mobile devices with cheap SD cards (as opposed to running on enterprise-grade SSDs), and corruptions are mo

• **westurner**：讨论了在SQLite中使用Merkle哈希来增强一致性和数据完整性的可能性，并提到了一些SQLite扩展和相关技术。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于SQLite的校验和功能是否应扩展以检测任意数据损坏，还是保持现有设计以防止部分写入和崩溃恢复。
• 对WAL校验和功能的正确理解和预期用途存在不同看法，部分评论者认为其设计合理并符合预期，而另一些评论者则希望看到更多错误通知和数据完整性检查功能。
• 提出了一些替代技术（如Merkle哈希）来增强SQLite的数据完整性，但这些技术涉及复杂的实现和权衡。

data.title: Mwm – The smallest usable X11 window manager
data.author: daureg
data.article_summary: mwm 是一个极简窗口管理器，专为追求最小化的用户设计。它仅有 20 行代码，不具备模式、美化界面、鼠标控制、虚拟桌面、配置文件等功能，窗口无标题栏、状态栏、按钮、边框和菜单，所有窗口全屏显示，一次只显示一个。它只包含最基本的功能：启动应用、切换窗口和关闭窗口。用户可以通过修改源码自定义键绑定，使用简单的 `grab` 和 `map` 宏。构建过程也很简单，运行 `./build.sh` 即可。mwm 强调软件应具备可 hack、有趣、小巧和可塑性强的特点，让用户能够轻松理解和修改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X11与Wayland生态的对比，以及对极简窗口管理器（WM）的讨论

不同观点：
• **X11的简便性与Wayland的复杂性**：一些用户（如trollied和ahlCVA）怀念X11的简单操作，如通过SSH和"export DISPLAY"轻松实现远程应用显示，而Wayland将窗口管理器和显示服务器绑定，使得新颖或实验性的窗口管理器更难发展和存活。即使有像wlroots这样的工具，开发者仍需投入更多精力才能实现X11中默认提供的功能。

• **对mwm（Motif Window Manager）的看法**：scoreandmore对mwm有深厚感情，认为它是完美的WM，并自1991年以来一直使用。然而，chasil指出mwm与Motif的命名冲突，并提到dtvwm在CDE中取代了mwm。pjmlp则在比较mwm与twn和uwm的大小。

• **对极简WM的讨论**：一些用户（如90s_dev和newlisp）欣赏极简WM的设计，认为现代软件常常过于臃肿，而极简WM展示了如何在保持功能和便利的同时实现最小化。90s_dev特别提到虽然现代软件有其存在的理由，但他个人倾向于使用和编写极简软件。

• **技术细节与代码实现**：90s_dev和ajross讨论了WM的源代码，赞赏其使用C宏实现的简洁和优雅。adxl认为代码易于阅读和理解，而yjftsjthsd-h则提到该WM类似于X11的cage。

补充讨论：
• **用户对资源的需求**：throwaway328询问是否有列出最小WM的资源页面，显示出对极简WM资源的兴趣。

• **兼容性问题**：teddyh指出该WM不符合ICCCM标准，这可能影响其在某些环境中的使用。

• **Wayland的可能性**：neoden提问是否能在Wayland中实现类似X11的极简WM功能，显示出对Wayland生态中极简WM潜力的关注。

争议焦点：
• **mwm命名冲突**：chasil指出mwm与Motif Window Manager的命名冲突，可能引起使用上的混淆。

• **X11与Wayland的优劣**：X11的简便性与Wayland的复杂性之间的对比是讨论的焦点，尤其是对于开发者和长期用户的影响。

mwm
The window manager for the true minimalist:
20 LOC.
No modes.
No "eye-candy".
No mouse control.
No virtual desktops.
No configuration files.
Not standards-compliant.
No title bars, no status bars, no buttons, no borders, no menus, etc.
All windows are full-screen, just one is visible at any given time.
Absolutely adaptable to your needs.
Includes just what is strictly needed.
This is the smallest, actually usable window manager I know about. Even
TinyWM is twice as large. However, it doesn't let you launch programs, or
assign key bindings.
mwm
does.
xterm
, with the
micro
editor, editing
mwm
's source.
Why?
Most software today is crappy. Do you really need all the bells and whistles?
Probably not.
We are in dire need of software that is hackable, fun, small, malleable, and
that you can wrap your head around, because: is it truly free software if, due
to its complexity, you cannot modify it? ;)
How?
The very essential things a window manager should let me do are:
Launch applications (which might create new windows).
Switch between windows.
Close windows.
Well, so that's all what
mwm
lets you do.
Two macros are available for assigning keybindings:
grab
and
map
. Read
mwm-custom.c
for an example on how to use them (my own setup).
You first need to
grab
the keys you want to be able to bind. Then you
map
them to actions.
Building.
Run
./build.sh
. Pass
CC=...
to use a different C compiler (I use
tcc
).
Dead simple.

data.title: UK: Phone networks down: EE, BT, Three, Vodafone, O2 not working in mass outage
data.author: oger
data.article_summary: 本文主要报道了英国多家主要电话网络（如BT、EE、Three和Vodafone）在某日下午发生大规模中断，导致数百万用户无法接打电话。用户在社交媒体上表达了 frustration，各公司发言人分别致歉并表示正在紧急修复问题。根据DownDetector地图，伦敦、伯明翰、曼彻斯特和格拉斯哥受影响最严重。O2用户虽有报告问题，但公司称其网络正常，问题源于其他运营商的故障。与此同时，《独立报》强调其在重要时刻进行深入报道的承诺，并呼吁读者支持其无付费墙的新闻服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国多家电信运营商（如BT/EE、Vodafone、O2）的服务中断问题及其可能原因

不同观点：
• **服务中断的确认与否认**：
   - **amiga386**：确认BT和EE存在问题，Vodafone和Three否认存在网络问题。O2的情况未知。
   - **MattPalmer1086**：没有察觉到问题，可能只影响部分网络，自己使用的Three网络正常。

• **可能的技术原因**：
   - **yabones**：猜测可能与2022年Rogers通信公司的大规模中断相似，可能是BGP（边界网关协议）配置错误。
   - **ivan_gammel**：联想到俄罗斯此前因“主权互联网”基础设施升级导致的中断，询问是否存在国家层面的基础设施更新。
   - **situationista**：猜测与Starlink的中断是否有关，尽管可能性不大，但时间点上的巧合值得注意。
   - **gandalfian**：Vodafone的MVNO数据正常，但无法打电话或发短信，O2和EE早期也无法打电话，但后来恢复正常。

• **用户体验与投诉**：
   - **rwmj**：BT的座机无拨号音，但通过Openreach的互联网正常。
   - **18172828286177**：质疑运营商没有及时向用户通报问题，指出对依赖电话的重要场景（如等待医生来电）可能造成影响。
   - **jonathantf2**：指出问题仅影响拨打EE号码的来电，如果号码已转网则不受影响。
   - **heraldgeezer**：文章未明确说明是语音、数据问题，还是两者皆有，且未说明涉及的网络代次（2G/3G/4G/5G），但多数投诉似乎与语音通话有关。

补充讨论：
• **对DownDetector的质疑**：
   - **chmod775**：指出DownDetector的报告地图可能仅反映人口密集区域的投诉，而非实际问题分布，质疑其准确性。
   - **wut42**：批评DownDetector夸大其词，认为其报道经常将小问题渲染成大规模中断。

• **其他猜测**：
   - **kerv**：开玩笑地问是否与Starlink有关。
   - **te_chris**：简单表示EE在伦敦正常。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点之一是服务中断的范围和影响程度，部分用户未察觉到问题，而其他用户则受到明显影响。
• 另一争议点是对DownDetector等第三方报告的可靠性，部分用户认为这些报告夸大或不准确。

总结：讨论围绕英国电信服务中断的技术原因、用户体验、运营商的沟通问题以及第三方报告的可靠性展开，反映了不同用户对同一事件的多种视角和体验。

Several major phone networks in the UK appear to be down following a major outage.
BT,
EE
, Three and
Vodafone
were all suffering issues on Thursday afternoon, according to Downdetector.
Millions of customers are unable to make or receive calls, with many taking to social media to report the problem.
“I can’t make or receive any calls,” one EE user
wrote
on X. “All I get is beep beep.”
A Vodafone user wrote: “I can’t get through to my dad.”
A spokesperson for Vodafone said the network is experiencing difficulties.
“We're really sorry, but due to some technical issues some customers will be experiencing issues making or receiving calls,” the spokesperson said.
“We know how important it is for you to have this working and we're working really hard to fix this as soon as possible.”
A representative for EE told several users on X that it is “looking into” the issue.
Outage map for EE
(
DownDetector
)
A map showing reports of EE outage reports made to DownDetector suggests that those in London, Birmingham, Manchester and Glasgow are the worst affected.
Some O2 customers reported issues, however a spokesperson for the company said that its network is operating “entirely as normal” today.
“The only reason behind the small spike on Down Detector – which is significantly smaller than other providers – is simply due to issues some of our customers might experience trying to contact friends or family who are with operators which are experiencing issues today,” the O2 spokesperson told
The Independent
. “It’s not an issue with our network.”

data.title: I wasted weeks hand optimizing assembly because I benchmarked on random data
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在一套分布式数据处理平台上进行Java优化工作的经历。目标系统运行于数十万台机器上，即便0.5%的性能提升也价值重大。作者面对的是高度优化的Java代码库，低效的部分早已被优化。通过分析，作者聚焦于数据序列化，尤其是VarInt编码的优化。尽管常规观点认为这类小优化无法通过原生代码提升，但作者通过手写无分支的SIMD汇编算法，实现了比Java版本快4倍的编码器。然而，在实际生产环境中测试时，发现优化效果并不明显。原因在于作者最初使用随机大数进行测试，而实际场景中的数字多为较小数值，导致Java版本在处理这些常见情况时表现并不差。最终，作者撤销了更改，将此次经历视为自定义JIT优化的概念验证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码优化和性能调优的不同方法及其实际效果

不同观点：
• MathMonkeyMan分享了Ken Thompson通过有限自动机优化代码的故事，但随后有人发现99.9%的请求都匹配某一特定策略，简单检查该策略即可大幅提升速度，这说明有时简单的优化比复杂的算法更有效。
• gorset介绍了在关键性能项目中使用fixedint32/64代替varint的优化方法，并指出这种方法在性能上很难被超越，但同时也提到新项目中使用SBE，虽然不如protobuf方便，但性能更优。
• jasonthorsness认为识别典型的使用场景并进行微基准测试非常困难，且容易导致时间和精力的浪费，提出目前还没有完美的解决方案，主要依赖于对测试设置的仔细思考。

44632674.article_content:
Once upon a time I worked in the field of Java Optimizations.
The target system was a distributed data processing platform that ran across hundreds of thousands of machines. At such scales, a 0.5% improvement would easily make up my salary going forward, and 2% was a good result for the half.
That doesn’t mean it was easy. Never have I ever seen such a highly optimized Java codebase. Not before, not since.
Every low hanging fruit had long since been picked clean. For example, there was minimal use of
java.lang.String
because ain’t nobody got time for a second allocation of a
char[]
with associated indirection and GC churn.
In other words, we were looking at increasingly heroic optimizations to justify our own existence.
Through careful, large scale profiling, I discovered that data serialization was a small but worthwhile place to focus. In particular, VarInt encoding used enough CPU time to warrant investigation.
If you’re not familiar, a VarInt, or more specifically ULEB128, is a byte efficient way to encode arbitrary integers. You use however many groups of 7 bits you need for your number, and use the 8th bit to specify whether there is another byte coming.
Numbers needing 7-bits or less (< 128) are encoded as
0nnnnnn
14-bit (<16384),
1nnnnnnn 0nnnnnnn
21bit (<2097152),
1nnnnnnn 1nnnnnnn 0nnnnnnn
And so on, in little-endian order.
For a 32bit int, you will need between 1 and 5 bytes. For a 64bit long, you will need between 1 and 10.
They are used in Google Protobuf, Apache/Facebook Thrift, WASM, DWARF, and other formats that want a compact binary representation without sacrificing range.
The interface the system used for this encoding was essentially
int encodeLong(byte[] buffer, int offset, long data)
, returning the number of bytes written.
Conventional wisdom is that this is way too small to benefit from native code.
But conventional wisdom is for conventional development.
We were in the early phases of forking the JVM, had recently built the infrastructure to implement custom optimizations, and we were itching to use it.
Engineers don’t exactly need convincing to work on fun assembly puzzles to begin with, but the empire builders in management were additionally competing in a Manifest Destiny style land grab as the company maneuvered to take control of its tech stack from end to end. They were pushing this as hard as anyone to stake their claims.
So off I went to write an ultra optimized VarInt encoder that the JVM JIT could serialize straight into the instruction stream, bypassing the normal overhead associated with JNI.
And I sure did.
My hand coded, branchless, SIMD assembly algorithm performed 4x better than the already highly optimized Java implementation!
(The exact details escape me, but it was some combination of using BMI2 to scatter bits into groups of 7, and some AVX2 comparisons and bit extensions to compute the continuation mask and determine the resulting length.)
This was verified in a benchmark that ran both versions on billions of random numbers, confirming both the huge speedup and the bit-for-bit compatibility of the result.
I spent probably two weeks implementing, testing, integrating, polishing, and landing this change.
Finally I tried to measure the difference in prod.
Nothing.
Measuring ~1% improvements is always a challenge, but even with huge A/B runs, the difference was exactly nothing.
I did some investigations, and eventually found why my benchmarks were so misleading compared to real world performance.
It was because I was using random numbers.
As it turns out, mathematically speaking, most numbers are huge. By an infinite margin. There are dramatically many more 18 digit numbers, than there are 3 digit numbers.
In fact, if you generate random 64bit unsigned longs and try to encode them as ULEB128,
50% will need 10 bytes
~49.6% will need 9 bytes
~0.38% will need 8 bytes
~0.003% will need 7 bytes
…
~0.00000000000009% will need 2 bytes
~0.0000000000000006% will need 1 byte
Meanwhile, if I look around my real world right now, I see several dozen numbers. Almost all fit into two bytes with room to spare. A “60” watt charger, an old Covid-“19” test, page “1” of “2” of some statement. A few zip codes and reference numbers break the pattern, but overall, real numbers tend to be small.
That’s exactly why people use VarInt in the first place.
The Java version had to do more work the more bytes it had to output. By measuring on random numbers, I was inadvertently doing all my testing against the algorithm’s unrealistic worst case scenario.
When I adjusted my benchmark to primarily generate small numbers, the speedup vanished entirely.
I ended up rolling back the change, and wrote off the time spent as a proof-of-concept for developing and productionizing a custom JIT optimization.
(And I crossed “SIMD” off my
programming bingo card
.)

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nia及相关工具的定价、功能、竞争优势及隐私问题

不同观点：
• **定价问题**：mtrovo认为Nia的定价策略可能难以被接受，尤其是需要额外支付文档访问费用。他觉得将多个MCP（Managed Coding Providers）打包在一起可能更具吸引力。
• **使用体验与方法**：efitz分享了自己通过AI生成文档的成功经验，并认为这种方法在多个项目中效果良好。
• **功能描述**：NiloCK指出Nia的标语不够具体，认为其描述的MCP服务器功能与其他类似服务没有明显区别。
• **竞争优势**：creepy和nisegami对Nia相对于Context7及CursorAI的竞争优势表示关注，质疑Nia的独特性及可替代性。
• **隐私与法律问题**：kokanator关心数据使用及隐私问题，对目前法律链接无效表示担忧。
• **性能提升**：afro88对Nia访问外部文档的能力表示疑问，想要了解哪些文档无法通过网络获取。
• **技术支持与版本控制**：taherchhabra提到在使用Claude编码时遇到的版本控制问题，询问Nia是否能解决此问题。
• **用户体验与网站问题**：chromehearts批评了Nia网站的性能，认为其加载速度慢。
• **开源问题**：smcleod询问Nia是否计划发布非商业用途的免费或开源版本。
• **价值评估**：fudged71对27%的性能提升表示质疑，想知道是否能达到10倍的改进。
• **文档整合功能**：EcommerceFlow建议增加一键集成最新文档的功能，质疑目前是否需要用户自行抓取和添加文档。

补充讨论：
• **工具对比与用户选择**：dcreater对Context7表示满意，询问Nia的优点；mvATM99则分享了使用GitMCP.io和Github Copilot的经验，认为其在文档和代理模式上有明显优势。
• **用户支持与社区反馈**：wohoodle表达了对Nia产品的兴趣，并鼓励继续开发，显示了用户对该产品的积极反馈和期待。

争议焦点：
• 定价策略是否合理，特别是额外文档访问费用的必要性。
• Nia相对于其他竞争产品的独特功能和竞争优势。
• 数据隐私和法律条款的透明度问题。

data.title: The POSIX specification of vi
data.author: exvi
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Unix系统中**vi**文本编辑器的基本功能和使用方法。vi是一个屏幕导向的文本编辑器，主要在支持用户可移植实用程序和POSIX2_CHAR_TERM符号的系统上提供。vi与行编辑器**ex**可以互换使用，用户可以在vi中执行ex命令。编辑操作在编辑缓冲区中进行，直到用户发出写文件命令才会实际修改文件。本文还描述了vi的选项、操作数、输入输出、环境变量及异步事件处理等细节。如果终端不支持某些vi功能，则可能默认进入ex模式。vi初始状态为命令模式，通过特定命令可以进入文本输入模式，并通过按**ESC**键返回命令模式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕文本编辑器及其与POSIX标准的合规性、使用和功能的讨论。

不同观点：
• Joker_vD认为使用"ed"文本编辑器比处理复杂的现代编辑器（如Vim）更为简单直接。
• gpvos指出Vim并非完全符合POSIX标准，因为它缺少开放模式（open mode），并提到自己曾在低速网络环境下使用该模式。
• webdevver将POSIX标准与Linux的关系比作网页标准与Chrome的关系，暗示POSIX标准可能不完全适用于所有Linux系统。
• wahern提供了一个链接，帮助用户探索POSIX标准，强调了该资源的价值。
• haunter提到华为的EulerOS是少数符合POSIX标准的Linux发行版之一，虽然是商业产品，但也有FOSS版本（openEuler）。
• nickandbro分享了自己因喜爱vi而开发的一个类似Vimgolf的应用，尽管底层使用了neovim，因为其API更易于使用。
• wpollock提醒用户Vim自带教程（vimtutor），并给出了在neovim中访问教程的方法。
• chasil提供了一个链接，帮助用户查看所有用户态实用程序，通过移除URL后缀实现。
• userbinator指出vi（以及ed和ex）已被POSIX标准指定，但emacs没有。
• eviks质疑配置快捷键的必要性，并询问用户更改快捷键是否违反POSIX标准。
• anthk提供了一个实际操作指南，教新手如何使用vi和nvi，并展示了基本命令的使用方法。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个文本编辑器，如ed、vi、nvi、Vim和neovim，用户对不同编辑器的偏好和使用场景有所不同。
• 对POSIX标准的合规性问题引起了多位用户的关注，尤其是Vim与POSIX标准之间的差异。
• 提供了一些实用资源和教程链接，帮助用户更好地理解和使用这些编辑器。
• 争议焦点之一是Vim是否完全符合POSIX标准，以及用户自定义快捷键是否违反POSIX标准。

44632783.article_summary: 本文介绍了Unix系统中**vi**文本编辑器的基本功能和使用方法。vi是一个屏幕导向的文本编辑器，主要在支持用户可移植实用程序和POSIX2_CHAR_TERM符号的系统上提供。vi与行编辑器**ex**可以互换使用，用户可以在vi中执行ex命令。编辑操作在编辑缓冲区中进行，直到用户发出写文件命令才会实际修改文件。本文还描述了vi的选项、操作数、输入输出、环境变量及异步事件处理等细节。如果终端不支持某些vi功能，则可能默认进入ex模式。vi初始状态为命令模式，通过特定命令可以进入文本输入模式，并通过按**ESC**键返回命令模式。

data.title: A valid HTML zip bomb
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对LLM（大型语言模型）网络爬虫的防御方法，使用了一种有效的HTML zip炸弹（zip bomb），通过消耗爬虫的资源来应对其过度抓取行为。传统的IP封锁难以奏效，因为爬虫使用分布式IP。作者设计了一种基于gzip和brotli压缩的HTML zip炸弹，利用HTML注释填充大量重复字符，实现1:1030的压缩比。该炸弹在解压时会耗尽爬虫的RAM资源，导致其崩溃。作者使用Nginx服务器配置，预压缩文件并通过HTTP头控制内容编码，确保炸弹仅对未遵守`robots.txt`的爬虫生效。实验表明，该方法能有效使Firefox和Chrome浏览器崩溃，但对合法爬虫通过`robots.txt`进行限制以避免误伤。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HTML zip炸弹的制作与效果，以及其对不同系统和浏览器的潜在影响

不同观点：
• [bhaney] 提出了一种制作HTML zip炸弹的方法，使用嵌套的<div>标签并通过gzip压缩，生成一个具有大量冗余数据的文件，用于对抗网络爬虫。

• [PeterStuer] 讨论了robots.txt文件的配置问题，指出很多配置并不合理，且自动获取robots.txt的行为可能会被识别为爬虫，导致需要采取额外措施（如通过VPN获取）以遵循其精神而非字面规则。

• [andrew_eu] 认为大型网络爬虫可能会忽略注释内容，建议在其他HTML元素中应用类似技巧，例如在样式标签中使用大量分号或在JS中定义巨大常量。还提到如果HTML包含大量链接指向其他zip炸弹，可能会放大对爬虫的影响。

• [chatmasta] 澄清提交的链接不是zip炸弹，点击是安全的。

• [Alifatisk] 和 [fdomingues] 都提到网页侧边栏在滚动时突然收起，导致内容左移的问题，表示这种设计不必要且影响阅读体验。

• [slig] 提问在使用Cloudflare的网站上应用这种方法会产生什么效果，是否会读取并缓存未压缩内容，或直接缓存并提供压缩文件。

• [Telemakhos] 和 [can16358p] 报告了在Safari浏览器上打开此类文件会导致WebKit错误。

• [cooprh] 甚至提到这种文件导致Safari上的1password崩溃。

• [xd1936] 表示这种链接点击起来有风险。

• [ranger_danger] 则表示在Linux上的Firefox和Chrome中并没有出现崩溃现象。

• [Tepix] 认为作为爬虫运营者，不太可能对这种文档有很大困扰。

补充讨论：
• [ChrisArchitect] 提到与gzip炸弹和电子邮件客户端的趣事，并提供了一个相关链接以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于这种HTML zip炸弹是否能有效对抗网络爬虫以及其对不同浏览器和系统的实际影响。一些人报告了崩溃和错误，而另一些人则没有遇到问题。此外，关于robots.txt文件的合理配置和遵循精神而非字面规则也存在讨论。

http web nginx zip-bomb compression security 2025-07-23T15:02:00.000 A valid HTML zip bomb Many sites have been affected by the aggressiveness of web crawlers designed to improve LLMs. I’ve been relatively spared, but since the phenomenon started, I've been looking for a solution to implement. Today, I present a zip bomb gzip and brotli that is valid HTML . LLM Web Crawlers The initial problem is the aggressiveness of LLM web crawlers that don't respect robots.txt . The first idea that comes to mind is IP blocking. However, web crawlers have circumvented this restriction by using individual IPs via specialized botnets. Another solution is therefore to exhaust the resources of the harvesters. With a zip bomb, we attempt to exhaust their RAM. 1 We’re exploiting the asymmetry of the resources needed to serve the zip bomb versus those needed to detect it. Naturally, I’m going to try to minimize the resources needed to distribute the zip bomb. A Gzip bomb The most basic gzip bomb consists of zeros. $ dd if =/dev/zero bs=1M count=10240 | gzip -9 > 10G.gzip That's not bad; the theoretical ratio is 1032:1 (approximately 1030 in practice for a zip bomb), so our file weighs ~10MiB. The problem is that web browsers parse the page on the fly as soon as possible and quickly detect that it's not a valid HTML page. So, I set myself the challenge of creating a valid HTML page containing a zip bomb. The HTML Zip Bomb I had several ideas. First, since it's an HTML page, we start with the HTML5 doctype. Then we try to fit the 10 MB of identical characters. I first attempted to use HTML classes, which can contain anything , but quickly the HTML comment solution seemed most practical. So, I set up a small shell script (in fish ) to create an HTML file with a 10 MB 'H' comment. #!/bin/fish # Base HTML echo -n 'Projet: Valid HTML bomb

This is a HTML valid bomb, cf. https://ache.one/articles/html_zip_bomb

" Then, we gzip all that: $ fish zip_bomb.fish | gzip -9 > bomb.html.gz $ du -sb bomb.html.gz 10180 bomb.html.gz We have our 1:1030 ratio, that’s perfect. Serving the Zip Bomb I use Nginx; the idea is to serve the pre-compressed file. Ideally, we don't even want the 10 GB file on the server. To do that, we use the ngx_http_gzip_static_module 2 . location = /bomb.html { gzip on ; # Normally this should be the gzip module on the fly. 🤷 gzip_static on ; gzip_proxied expired no -cache no -store private auth; gunzip off ; # Definitely don't decompress the gzip! brotli_static on ; # My site is available in brotli too, so why not. } Unfortunately, Nginx returns a 404 if the bomb.html file doesn't exist, so I created a small, simple file that announces that it’s a gzip bomb. $ curl https://ache.one/bomb.html You don't support gzip encoding. Add the HTTP header "accept-encoding: gzip". I verify that Nginx is serving the file correctly: $ curl -H "accept-encoding: gzip,br" -I -- https://ache.one/bomb.html | grep content content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 content-length: 8298 content-encoding: br $ curl -H "accept-encoding: gzip" -I -- https://ache.one/bomb.html | grep content content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 content-length: 10420650 content-encoding: gzip Okay, the size is right. Now we absolutely must make sure that we don’t exceed the budget of a legitimate web crawler by forbidding it in robots.txt. By placing it at the root, I know that my robots.txt already forbids it, but otherwise, we should find this: User-agent: * Disallow: /bomb.html Results Firefox struggles a lot and ends up crashing cleanly with an NS_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY error, visible only in the developer tools. If I put the body tag before the malicious comment, I would certainly have a correctly displayed page. Chrome is much faster to crash! It offers a happy screen signaling that an error occurred via SIGKILL . In both cases, we notice that the page is partially loaded; however, the title is correct. Therefore, we are certain that a Selenium-type web crawler will crash on this HTML file. Fortunately, there appears to be no security vulnerability to exploit. Evolution The HTML comment trick is certainly not the most elegant. I’m sure there are plenty of ideas to fit packs of 258 identical characters 3 . However, here it seems to work so well that I haven’t taken the time to explore further. The interest of having a more varied HTML zip bomb would be to ensure that the HTML parser doesn’s optimize the reading of certain parts. By the way, I allowed myself to create a brotli version as

data.title: When swiping supplants scissors: The hidden cost of touchscreens
data.author: SLHamlet
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了触屏设备对儿童精细运动技能发展的影响。作者Amber Case指出，过度使用触摸屏导致许多孩子在使用铅笔、剪刀和系鞋带等基本动作上遇到困难。这种从实体互动向虚拟互动的转变，减少了孩子们通过动手学习的机会。作者结合自身童年通过手工和早期计算机学习的经历，强调了触觉互动对儿童发展的重要性。她呼吁设计师和公司通过恢复更多触觉体验来帮助孩子们更好地成长，例如在教育中增加手工和艺术活动。文章最后提醒，技术进步不应以牺牲儿童的基本发展技能为代价。

44672145.article_content:
When Swiping Supplants Scissors: The Hidden Cost of Touchscreens — and how Designers Can Help
Amber Case
9 min read
·
1 day ago
--
Listen
Share
Zoom image will be displayed
The history of technology is full of innovators who got their start creating with their hands. Steve Jobs cites a calligraphy class at Reed College as influencing the design of the Mac;
Susan Kare
, who designed the Apple icons we still use today, had a childhood immersed in arts, crafts, and embroidery.
It’s a keen irony that their work evolved into smartphones and tablets — devices that have inadvertently led to a whole generation whose primary mode of interaction is a flat glass touchscreen. I was shocked to
to recently read
how much a
lack of physical tactility is affecting fine motor skills of kids:
A recent survey by
Education Week
found that 77 percent of educators reported young students having greater difficulties handling pencils, pens, and scissors. In comparison, 69 percent noted increased struggles with tying shoes compared to five years ago.
Children are losing critical fine motor skills — the small, precise movements required to tie a shoelace, write with a pen, or build a tower.
“It’s like they’ve never seen a block,” says Hornbeck, an instructional coach at Beverly City Public Schools in New Jersey, describing how kids fumble when asked to stack just three blocks. “The things they do with the block when you’ve just shown them what to do is boggling.”
It’s painful for me to picture a kid struggling to use scissors, trying to coordinate their small hands to work two blades at the same time.
The shift away from the tactile is so profound, I’m beginning to explore it with some first-hand reporting for an upcoming project. In this essay, I’ll share some of my early findings, contrast them with my own childhood experiences, then conclude with some principles and research that I hope inspire designers and companies to help restore tactile interactivity in our lives.
Chromebooks for Kids — But Few Paintbrushes
I recently interviewed Cathy, a veteran teacher with over 30 years of teaching experience at elementary school in Salem, Oregon about what she’s seen in classrooms over time.
Zoom image will be displayed
A photo of a child enrolled in Salem, Oregon’s school district with a chromebook (
Photo credit
).
Cathy told me that the school’s
Kindergarteners
now get Chromebooks “to keep up with the times
”.
She explained:
They have little badges, like they have their password on them, and they just wave it in front of the Chrome Chromebook [so] they don’t have to memorize all that early on. Kindergarten is more like first grade now, and it used to be like a preschool, I would say now it’s advanced to first grade level, and first grade is like second grade, and everything’s accelerated.
She also added that visual arts and crafts aren’t keeping up with this shift; there was only a
single
painting project during the entire last semester at her school.
Zoom image will be displayed
A kid painting as part of Learning to Draw and Paint: A Natural Process (
Image credit
)
Our need for touch is fundamental to how we engage with the world. The human mind expects texture and tactility. It helps us orient ourselves to the world and use objects more easily. When we ignore crafts that engage hands and not just eyes, we reduce opportunities for kids to learn spatially and effectively.
How a Childhood of Crafts & Early Computers Shaped Me
When I was little, my room had very few toys. I had LEGOs and some matchbox cars, and was encouraged to figure out how to use cardboard, tape, and scissors to make more toys of my own. It taught me to problem solve and work with as little resources as possible.
I think back to my dad teaching me how to
solder circuitboards
before I even got to preschool. He told me all about how to hold the soldering iron, months before he allowed me to hold it. When he saw that my hand-eye coordination was strong enough, I assisted him in building the circuit boards. These were huge moments for me. My dad was teaching me alongside his own, professional work. He treated me like an adult, while also being careful to understand my own level as a growing kid.
I am certain all of this learning and creating with my hands contributed to any success I later earned throughout my career in technology.
Zoom image will be displayed
My dad showing me how to test speaker equiptment in my childhood backyard in 1989.
I also think back to getting my first personal computer, in my early teens, and how much it changed me. It replaced my backyard and my construction tools. I started to stay up late. It affected my sleep. While it consumed more and more of my time, I drew less. I was less happy. The information on the screen was exciting, but it wasn’t satisfactory. I felt like I had eaten so much information, but I didn’t feel full.
Fortunately I started out with an early childhood of tactile creativity, and know why I need to return to it. Sometime

data.title: Psilocybin treatment extends cellular lifespan, improves survival of aged mice
data.author: atombender
data.article_summary: 一项由埃默里大学主导的研究发现，迷幻蘑菇中的活性成分裸盖菇素（psilocybin）及其代谢物裸盖菇醇（psilocin）可能具有抗衰老和促进精神健康的益处。研究显示，裸盖菇醇能延长人类皮肤和肺细胞的寿命超过50%。在小鼠实验中，定期低剂量服用裸盖菇素使小鼠寿命延长30%，并改善了毛发质量和减少白发。该研究表明，裸盖菇素通过减少氧化应激、改善DNA修复反应和保持端粒长度，影响衰老过程，可能为抗衰老疗法带来革命性变化。研究人员强调需进一步研究其在老年人群中的系统性影响，以提升生活质量和健康老龄化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于研究中使用裸盖菇素对寿命延长效果的讨论，以及对实验设计和剂量的质疑。

不同观点：
• [awanderingmind] 认为研究结果中寿命延长的效果过大，怀疑是否存在未控制的混杂因素。特别指出研究人员未对分组进行盲法处理，可能影响结果。
• [andoando] 对剂量换算提出疑问，最初计算错误后进行了修正，认为人类等效剂量与研究中提到的剂量存在差异。
• [mekoka] 对研究中使用的剂量表示怀疑，特别是将5mg/kg视为低剂量。通过对比约翰·霍普金斯大学的数据，认为此剂量过高。但也通过进一步计算和考虑脑大小因素，认为剂量可能合理。此外，提出研究结果可能与“旅行”体验有关，而非单纯化学物质的作用。
• [kubb] 对实际应用中的口味问题表示关注，但总体上对使用裸盖菇素持积极态度。
• [fny] 提出SSRIs是否会有类似效果的疑问，质疑是否只要是血清素影响衰老过程，其来源是否重要。
• [gooodvibes] 表示即使药物缩短寿命，也仍然值得使用，显示出对研究结果的乐观态度。
• [puppycodes] 以幽默方式提到药物可能带来的副作用，暗示对长期使用效果的担忧。
• [evanjrowley] 对现代医学和药物研究持阴谋论观点，认为研究结果可能被利用以牟利。
• [foobarian] 质疑延长寿命的实际意义，担心药物可能导致的精神失能时间超过其带来的寿命延长。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是研究中使用的剂量是否合理，以及实验设计中的盲法处理不足可能带来的影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是裸盖菇素对衰老的影响是否必须依赖于其致幻效果，还是化学物质本身具有独立作用。
• 不同的评论者对研究结果的态度从积极到怀疑各异，显示出对该领域研究的复杂看法。

44675708.article_content:
Main content
Psilocybin, the active ingredient in psychedelic mushrooms, may have both anti-aging as well as mental health benefits.
— Getty Images, 24K-Production
As revenues from the anti-aging market — riddled with hope and thousands of supplements — surged past $500 million last year, Emory University researchers identified a compound that actively delays aging in cells and organisms.
A
newly published study
in Nature Partner Journals’ Aging demonstrates that psilocin, a byproduct of consuming psilocybin, the active ingredient in psychedelic mushrooms, extended the cellular lifespan of human skin and lung cells by more than 50%.
In parallel, researchers also conducted the first long-term
in vivo
study evaluating the systemic effects of psilocybin in aged mice of 19 months, or the equivalent of 60–65 human years.
Results indicated that the mice that received an initial low dose of psilocybin of
5 mg/kg
, followed by a monthly high dose of
15 mg/kg for 10 months
, had a 30% increase in survival compared to mice who hadn’t received any.
These mice also displayed healthier physical features, such as improved fur quality, fewer white hairs and hair regrowth.
While traditionally researched for its mental health benefits, this study suggests that psilocybin impacts multiple hallmarks of aging by reducing oxidative stress, improving DNA repair responses, and preserving telomere length. Telomeres are the structured ends of a chromosome, protecting it from damage that could lead to the formation of age-related diseases, such as cancer, neurodegeneration or cardiovascular disease. These foundational processes influence human aging and the onset of these chronic diseases.
Louise Hecker, PhD, senior author of the study
The study concludes that psilocybin may have the potential to revolutionize anti-aging therapies and could be an impactful intervention in an aging population.
“Most cells in the body express serotonin receptors, and this study opens a new frontier for how psilocybin could influence systemic aging processes, particularly when administered later in life,” says Louise Hecker, PhD, senior author on the study, and former associate professor at Emory, where the research was initiated and funded.
While much of what researchers know about psilocybin relates to the brain, few studies have examined its systemic impacts. Many people associate psilocybin with the hallucinogenic impacts, but the majority of the cells in the body express serotonin receptors.
“Our study opens new questions about what long-term treatments can do. Additionally, even when the intervention is initiated late in life in mice, it still leads to improved survival, which is clinically relevant in healthy aging,” adds Hecker, currently an associate professor at Baylor College of Medicine.
Not just a longer life, but a healthier life
This news comes on the heels of KFF’s
recent report
that U.S. life expectancy is still below that of other countries similar in income and size, with an average lifespan of 78.4 years, compared to 82.5 years elsewhere. Not only was it the lowest, but as the lifespan in similar countries increased by 7.9 years from 1980-2022, the U.S. life expectancy has only increased by 4.7 years.
Ali Zarrabi, co-investigator of the study
“This study provides strong preclinical evidence that psilocybin may contribute to healthier aging — not just a longer lifespan, but a better quality of life in later years,” says
Ali John Zarrabi
, MD, director of psychedelic research at Emory's Department of Psychiatry. “As a palliative care physician-scientist, one of my biggest concerns is prolonging life at the cost of dignity and function. But these mice weren’t just surviving longer — they experienced better aging,” adds Zarrabi, co-investigator of the study.
Zarrabi emphasizes the importance of further research in older adults, as well as the well-documented overlap between physical and mental health.
“Emory is actively involved in Phase II and III clinical trials of psilocybin-assisted therapy for depression, and these results suggest we also need to understand psilocybin’s systemic effects in aging populations,” says Zarrabi. “My hope is also that if psilocybin-assisted therapy is approved as an intervention for depression by the FDA in 2027, then having a better quality of life would also translate into a longer, healthier life.”
The study was initiated at Emory University and funded by several awards, including the Imagine, Innovative, and Impact (I3) Award, Emory University School of Medicine; the Georgia CTSA NIH Award; and a grant from Emory’s Woodruff Health Sciences Center for Health in Aging.

data.title: Inter-Planetary Network Special Interest Group
data.author: OhMeadhbh
data.article_summary: IPNSIG（互联网协会星际分会）由Vint Cerf及学术界和NASA/JPL研究人员于1998年创立，目标是将地球网络扩展至太阳系空间，实现“互联网普及太空，惠及全人类”的愿景。其工作包括发展延迟与中断容忍网络（DTN），建立太阳系互联网架构与治理，并通过报告和策略推动相关技术成熟。该组织致力于连接未开发区域，促进星际网络的共同愿景和未来规划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：星际网络和Starlink相关技术问题及解决方案

不同观点：
• OhMeadhbh认为，在Starlink出现问题时，可以回顾Vint Cerf在1998年创立的IPN SIG（星际互联网协议特别兴趣小组），该小组讨论高延迟和可能的高损耗链路上的IP协议问题。他还提到希望看到更多关于信息安全的用例。

• webdevver用幽默的方式暗示Comcast可能会“意外地”通过“碎片”摧毁Starlink卫星链路，隐含对Starlink可靠性的质疑。

• LorenDB认为，星际网络最可能的解决方案是在距离现有数据中心几光秒以外的地方投入大量数据中心和计算资源，并使用类似IPFS的技术在行星间进行数据同步。

• rippeltippel自称是DTNPerf（用于DTN的iperf）初始版本的作者，提到自己已经转向其他软件工程领域，但很高兴看到DTN技术仍被关注，并指出ESA（欧洲航天局）也在研究该技术。

• ieee-e以讽刺的语气评论帖子中图形太多，单间距字体太少，暗示对讨论的专业性质疑，并附上一个指向RFC 1的链接。

• t1234s提出一个开放性问题，询问量子纠缠是否可以消除网络延迟，暗示对未来技术解决方案的探索。

• jibal分享个人经历，提到自己曾与Vint Cerf在UCLA共事，称赞Vint Cerf是个很酷的人，侧面支持对Vint Cerf及其工作的认可。

• userulluipeste对“Solar System”的写法提出小修正，强调应大写，因为这是专有名词，指出我们居住的太阳系应被准确描述。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术概念，包括IPN（星际网络协议）、DTN（延迟容忍网络）、量子纠缠和IPFS（星际文件系统），显示出对不同技术方案的探讨。
• 评论中存在幽默和讽刺（如webdevver和ieee-e的评论），以及对技术细节的认真探讨（如rippeltippel和LorenDB的评论），形成轻松但富有深度的讨论氛围。
• 争议焦点不明显，但存在对技术实现方式的不同看法，比如LorenDB和rippeltippel对星际网络解决方案的不同视角。

44675553.article_content:
IPNSIG works to expand the Internet into space
Learn more
IPNSIG was founded in 1998 by Vint Cerf and researchers within academia and NASA/JPL. We are now a full Chapter within the Internet Society, known as the Interplanetary Chapter. We work to extend terrestrial networking into solar system space, which is consistent with the Internet Society’s objectives to grow the internet to unpopulated areas, and connect the unconnected domain—and to ensure that even in space, “The Internet is for Everyone”.
Learn About Delay and Disruption Tolerant Networking
Read about how we can build and manage the Solar System Internet in
our Architecture and Governance report.
Get the report here
Read about our strategy toward a solar system Internet for humanity
Get the Strategy Working Group report
here
OUR VISION
Expand networking to interplanetary space,
for the benefit of humanity
CREATING
VISION
Create a common vision for an Interplanetary Network with stakeholders
NARRATIVE AND ROADMAP
Shape the future of an Interplanetary Network by presenting a narrative and roadmap
PROMOTION OF TECHNOLOGY
Promote and increase the maturity of DTN Technology through use in terrestrial and space application

data.title: American sentenced for helping North Koreans get jobs at U.S. firms
data.author: fortran77
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一位女性为朝鲜黑客提供工作机会事件的看法及相关安全问题的讨论

不同观点：
• WorldPeas认为文章遗漏了该女性曾经的无家可归经历，这可能是她做出此行为的原因之一。他们认为该女性并非不可同情的叛徒，她的行为更多是出于无知，并认为这种情况可能在其他未涉及国家行为者的案例中也发生过。
• ericzawo用讽刺的语气表达了对朝鲜黑客比他们自己更容易找到工作的惊讶。
• rdtsc猜测该女性可能不完全了解自己行为的后果，或者认为只是帮助了一些“好人”找工作，而不是故意参与重大犯罪活动。
• yardie以幽默的方式评论了雇佣顶级开发者的情况。
• sampton认为一个人不可能独自完成所有面试和沟通工作，建议还不如自己成立一个代理公司。
• 0cf8612b2e1e提出一个严肃的问题，如果该女性是为美国或德国人工作，会面临什么样的指控和判决。
• throwmeaway222以幽默的方式回应了关于身份验证的讨论。
• walrus01从信息安全角度分析了企业远程工作笔记本电脑的安全问题，指出远程桌面软件或KVM over IP设备可能带来的风险，并建议加强端点安全策略。
• globalnode认为应该更好地照顾弱势群体，以防止此类事件的发生，并提出这是一种支持社会主义的论据。
• standardUser对该女性仅被判8年半表示惊讶，认为这算是“轻微的叛国”。
• MrCoffee7提供了另一个非付费墙的文章链接，供大家阅读更多关于此案的信息。
• valbaca认为该女性帮助朝鲜政府从美国公司获取资金，应被以叛国罪起诉。
• mosferatu质疑为什么朝鲜被当作恶棍，而中国被视为更大的威胁却没有受到同样的关注。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于该女性的行为是否出于无知以及她是否应该被以叛国罪起诉。
- 信息安全问题被多次提及，特别是企业远程工作设备的安全策略。
- 有人对朝鲜作为威胁的严重性提出质疑，认为中国才是更大的威胁。
- 不同评论者对该事件的法律后果和道德评价存在分歧。

data.title: Working on a Programming Language in the Age of LLMs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在LLM（大型语言模型）时代继续开发编程语言（如Rye）的意义和挑战。作者承认LLM可以从提示生成代码，并且这种技术正在改变编程领域，甚至可能最终取代一些传统编程语言。然而，作者认为，专门的编程语言提供了自然语言无法达到的精确性和特定性，是解决复杂计算问题的关键工具。LLM依赖过去的解决方案，缺乏真正的创新能力，而专门语言不仅是交流工具，更是帮助思考和解决问题的认知框架。因此，作者坚信继续开发像Rye这样的编程语言仍有其价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）对新编程语言采用的影响及编程语言设计的未来

不同观点：
• **[amccollum]**：由于LLM是基于互联网上的现有代码进行训练的，如果所有人都用LLM来写代码，那么新编程语言将很难被LLM支持，因为没有新代码被写出来，这形成了一个自我强化的循环。以Zig语言为例，由于该语言发展迅速，LLM生成的代码常常基于过时的版本，导致错误。对于一些更为晦涩的语言（如Faust），LLM的表现也非常差。

• **[seunosewa]**：LLM可以被用来教人们如何使用新的编程语言，从而促进新语言的采用。

• **[sshine]**：引用了多个项目和博客，指出像Python和TypeScript这样的输出语言在LLM中表现更好是意料之中的。讨论了是否应该创建LLM无法合成的语言，并认为编程作为一种娱乐活动本身是有价值的，即使语言不被广泛使用。

• **[AllegedAlec]**：提到Alan Kay的工作，尤其是STEPS项目，该项目专注于为特定问题领域创建DSL（领域特定语言）。例如，通过ASCII图表和表格实现TCP。认为这种方法可能对当前问题有所帮助。

• **[dustingetz]**：引用“Notational Intelligence”文章，认为符号表示法的价值在于使我们能够处理新的抽象。更好的符号表示法可以帮助我们处理更复杂的概念和想法。编程语言的重点就是提供这种符号表示法。

• **[blamestross]**：LLM作为序列的自动编码器，能够写出低熵值的代码。这意味着存在更高效的结构可以用于编程。现有的编程语言并非最佳选择，我们需要自己去发现或创造更适合我们意图的编程语言。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于新编程语言是否能在LLM时代得到广泛采用。一方认为LLM的训练数据限制了新语言的发展，另一方认为LLM可以被用来促进新语言的学习和使用。
• 讨论中还涉及了编程语言设计的核心价值，包括符号表示法的重要性以及寻找更高效编程结构的必要性。
• 提到的具体项目和资源（如LMQL、Sudolang、STEPS）提供了实际例子，展示了当前在编程语言设计和LLM结合方面的探索。

44640471.article_content:
Table of Contents
genie
buzz
killing
specific
thoughts
yesterday’s
monkeys
genie
#
I’ve been working on
Rye
since 2018. It’s a project of joy — but also because I believe there is a potential to create something of value to others, eventually.
Even people living under a rock know we’ve entered the
age of LLMs
. I don’t jump to ships too soon, but eventually, even I had to admit:
code
can
get generated from prompts. And in many situations — with a smart prompter — the results are
quite OK
.
Even if you disagree,
genie
can’t be put back in the bottle. Technical progress generally only moves forward.
buzz
#
Trying to persuade programmers to switch to a language you made up is very ambitious (or just mad) on its own. When all the
buzz
is about not needing to use any programming language
at all, it makes even less sense.
The falling tide lowers all boats — and my is not even in the water yet.
killing
#
LLMs currently need programming languages, they can’t just generate executables directly from your prompt. Absurdly they also need examples, tutorials, blogposts, Stack Overflow answers,
which they are now well,
killing
.
LLMs are on the level of transpiler languages (Coffeescript?). They need the host languages — but if really succsessful, they would end up killing the host.
If no one uses Python anymore, will anyone still work on Python? (Just an example.)
Probably, in the long term, LLMs* will have/generate their own runtimes, libraries, and everything else. (* Or what comes next.)
specific
#
So the real question —
does it make sense to keep developing Rye?
— boils down to:
Is natural language the best substrate to declare what you want from a computer?
Traditionally, programmers believed it isn’t. But maybe it’s a matter of
specificity
.
Yes, natural language can be used to declare any solution — but it’s not ideal for declaring a
specific
one.
“Make me a Flutter app where I can jot down recipes and rate them”
vs.
Specific storage. Specific structures. Specific behavior. Specific interface…
Specialized languages—with consistent, exact, and repeatable design—will beat natural language at that.
Like any specialized tool beats a general one at the task it’s built for.
thoughts
#
Languages are not just tools for communication. They are also tools for
thinking
.
Medical jargon helps doctors communicate, store information — and also think about medical issues.
SQL helps us think about data and its relationships.
Functional languages help us solve problems that compose better and cleaner (with less state).
These aren’t just syntax choices — they’re
cognitive frameworks
.
If we lose tools for precise thought, we may lose the ability to have precise
thoughts
altogether.
yesterday’s
#
LLMs are trained on
yesterday’s
solutions
. They are good at recombining existing patterns, even in novel ways, but they are fundamentally backward-looking.
If we stop developing better ways of expressing computational ideas — is this it?
Does progress stop here?
monkeys
#
This also leads to a question (inspired by certain
monkeys
on typewriters) I asked LLMs a few times:
If you leave 100 LLMs chatting for 100 years, will they come up with any original thought?
Or would they simply recombine existing knowledge in increasingly sophisticated ways — trapped in an echo chamber of human-generated training data?
Ask your favorite LLM.
And yes — I still think it makes sense to build a language. Maybe more than ever.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创业公司收购中的薪酬和股权分配问题，特别是员工在收购中的待遇和股权兑现问题。

不同观点：
• **强调薪资而非股权**：[stan_kirdey] 认为工程师应争取更高的基本工资，因为股权往往不值钱。他建议员工要求公司提供409A估值、清算优先权和薪资区间，以获得更多透明度。
• **管理层和员工之间的不平等**：[CalChris] 指出在收购中，管理层和投资者通过谈判获得了优先权，而普通员工则往往得不到应有的回报。
• **对员工的偏见**：[chambers] 提到Garry Tan的推文（后被删除）反映了对员工的不公平待遇，偏向管理层和创始人。
• **收购中的实际收益**：[KaiserPro] 分享了自己被FAANG收购的经历，指出收购公告中的数字往往具有误导性，员工实际获得的收益远低于表面数字，且通常通过“金色手铐”方式分期支付。
• **创始人的人品决定结果**：[BhavdeepSethi] 认为选择加入创业公司时，创始人的人品比公司本身更重要。优秀的创始人会确保员工有好的结果，即使公司表现一般。
• **具体情况具体分析**：[lemax] 认为Windsurf的案例不具有普遍性，因为其产品易于复制且缺乏护城河。但仍有创业公司拥有有价值的IP和忠实客户群，能带来更好的退出结果。
• **软件开发的不道德现象**：[mawadev] 提到员工在软件开发中往往被视为可替换的“细胞”，即使提供了巨大价值，实际收益却很少，强调只有银行账户里的钱才是真实的。

补充讨论：
• **对推文内容的困惑**：[crazygringo] 对推文内容表示困惑，尤其是关于员工在收购中被迫放弃已兑现股份的情况，其他评论者也表示类似困惑。
• **成功的股权兑现案例**：[cleandreams] 分享了自己在FAANG收购中获得30万美元的股权兑现，并通过投资实现了财务自由。
• **法律诉讼的可能性**：[jschveibinz] 认为Windsurf的员工应通过法律手段追究创始人的责任，尤其是当所有价值都在员工身上时。
• **对百分比的怀疑**：[skybrian] 对推文中提到的1%的股权兑现表示怀疑，认为没有提供足够的数字信息。
• **对大公司工作条件的批评**：[whiplash451] 指出大公司的工作条件也变得糟糕，且仍存在支付稳固基本薪资的优质创业公司。

争议焦点：
• **员工在收购中是否应获得更多透明度和公平待遇**：推文和评论中多次提到员工在收购中往往得不到透明信息和公平回报，尤其是与管理层和投资者相比。
• **股权兑现的强制性问题**：员工是否可以被迫放弃已兑现的股权，以及在何种情况下会被要求这样做，是讨论中的一个主要争议点。

通过这些观点，可以看出在创业公司收购中，员工、管理层和投资者之间的利益分配存在显著不平衡，尤其是在股权和薪酬透明度方面。

data.title: A GPU Calculator That Helps Calculate What GPU to Use
data.author: chlobunnee
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VRAM计算器的有效性、功能和局限性，以及对不同硬件（如NVIDIA和AMD）的支持。

不同观点：
• **支持特定计算器的观点**：[zargon]认为https://apxml.com/tools/vram-calculator 更全面，特别是它能够理解不同模型的注意力机制，并支持量化和KV缓存的计算。但也提到该工具仅支持特定模型，而通用计算器由于模型架构差异往往不准确。

• **对计算器准确性的批评**：[kouteiheika]指出该计算器对训练内存的估算极不准确，尤其是在FP32、BF16、8-bit Adam等技术使用上。例如，训练14B参数模型实际仅需24GB VRAM，而计算器却估算3.77B参数模型需要62GB VRAM。[kouteiheika]认为通过一些优化技巧可以大幅降低VRAM使用。

• **对计算器实用性的质疑**：[funfunfunction]认为该工具可能是为GPU经销商做的廉价营销噱头，暗示其可信度不高。

• **对AMD支持的关注**：[amstan]和[jjmarr]等提到该计算器缺少对AMD硬件的支持，并指出在实际使用中AMD硬件可以运行大型模型，而Nvidia GPU却不一定足够，这显示了对更多硬件支持的需求。

• **对模型选择的困惑**：[mdaniel]对需要手动输入大量模型数据表示困惑，并认为计算结果不明确，降低了工具的实用性。

• **对具体GPU型号缺失的疑问**：[amanzi]和[timothyduong]提到某些具体GPU型号（如RTX 5060 Ti和3090）未被提及，质疑它们是否适用或为何被排除。

• **对计算器功能的建议**：[daft_pink]建议增加导入标准模型的功能，以便用户了解运行流行模型所需的GPU。[chlobunnee]则介绍了自己开发的计算器，并寻求反馈，希望进一步改进功能。

data.title: Revisiting Moneyball
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 《Moneyball》讲述了2002年奥克兰运动家队在低预算下凭借数据分析（特别是上垒率OBP）取得成功的故事。球队总经理比利·比恩和统计学家保罗·德波德斯塔利用赛伯计量学挑战传统球探方法，通过客观数据如OBP做出球员选择，使决策更加透明和可量化。例如，他们以低价签下斯科特·哈特伯格，并通过让他改守一垒，充分发挥其上垒能力。运动家队在该年取得了103场胜利，并创下20场连胜的纪录，验证了数据分析策略的有效性。然而，随着运动家队离开奥克兰，该策略也被批评为导致低薪资预算，并被认为夸大了数据分析对比赛结果的影响。文章回顾了《Moneyball》的核心主题及其对体育界的持久影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Moneyball策略及其在体育和商业中的应用与影响

不同观点：
• **thom**：认为分析技术能帮助聪明的组织提升表现，但并不能保证成功。不够成熟的组织可能会因为确认偏误而失败，而中间群体的好工作常常被决策者忽视。

• **timshell**：Moneyball的核心教训不是单纯的分析，而是系统性地评估被低估的资产。在"后Moneyball时代"，传统球探方法重新受到重视，结合分析和传统方法才能获得市场优势。

• **cainxinth**：指出数据统计上季后赛表现不一定反映球队的真实水平，但球迷直觉上更看重季后赛表现，两者之间存在认知差异。

• **rsync**：通过巴西柔术的例子说明在比赛中坚持有效的策略是关键，但非分析派的球探更具人性化，可能在工作中获得更多乐趣。

• **johnnienaked**：运用博弈论的观点，指出如果只有一人使用Moneyball策略，它是一个竞争优势，但随着策略普及，这种优势会逐渐消失。

• **hhmc**：关注棒球比赛中本垒打、保送和三振增加的现象，质疑棒球规则是否需要改变以增加比赛的紧凑性和观赏性。

• **ryukoposting**：认为"Moneyball"这个名称引发了关于低薪支付球员的争议，但指出MLB近年来在缓解“三种真实结果”问题上做得不错，比如引入投球时钟。

• **alexpotato**：分享了自己在大学 paintball 中应用Moneyball策略的经验，强调分析技术不仅在于识别如上垒率等指标，更在于发现被低估的指标并应用它们。

• **hx8**：认为Moneyball的核心在于识别和展示被低估的资产在竞争环境中的价值，因在棒球中的应用而广泛传播。

• **xbar**：质疑谁误解了Moneyball的真正含义。

• **readthenotes1**：提出不超额支付明星球员而是雇佣能够完成工作的人是否是一种反劳工行为的问题。

补充讨论：
- Moneyball策略的应用与争议，包括对球员的低薪支付和市场效率问题。
- 传统方法与现代分析技术的结合，以及如何在不同领域中找到平衡点。
- 对棒球规则的潜在修改以改善比赛的节奏和观赏性。
- 分析技术在识别被低估指标中的实际应用与效果。

Revisiting Moneyball
Data, sports, payrolls, and memes
Pardis Noorzad

Oakland Coliseum, September 2022.
Why are we
still
talking about Moneyball? Why am
I
talking about Moneyball?
For one, I’ve been meaning to write this post since 2019.
2018
even.
Zoom image will be displayed
My friends are the best. From
here
.
The
book
was published in 2003, and the
movie
was released in 2011. It feels silly to rehash, except the whole thing fascinates fans two decades later. Why? On the one hand, it is loved because it tells the classic underdog story while suggesting that nerdy analytics contributed to the wins; on the other, and especially as the A’s leave Oakland, it is blamed for encouraging low payrolls and critiqued for overstating the impact of analytics on the 2002 season and beyond.
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
From
here
,
here
, and
here
.
In this post, I’ll go over
the author
’s intentions for writing the book, followed by popular critiques of Moneyball. The goal is to address some of the recurring debates as we cover the main themes and provide historical context for each.
Understanding Moneyball
Let’s begin by discussing the book’s central themes and what the author found intriguing about the A’s in 2002. Moneyball has been so influential that many of these themes have since become memes.
Analytics leads to more transparent decision-making.
The A’s GM, Billy Beane, working with statistician Paul DePodesta, used sabermetrics to challenge traditional scouting methods that relied on more subjective evaluations.
This transparency allowed decisions regarding players to be justified through objective metrics. When the A’s signed Scott Hatteberg or traded for David Justice, they could point to specific evidence, like on-base percentage (OBP) or plate discipline, to justify their decision. This approach also aimed to make decision makers accountable for outcomes by establishing a decision-making framework that could be communicated, replicated, and thus improved upon.
Getting on base is undervalued, and teams can use this to their advantage.
While scouts focused on batting average, home runs, and RBIs, Beane recognized that OBP had a stronger correlation with run production than any of the traditional metrics. [1][2]
Zoom image will be displayed
The math was simple: teams that get on base more frequently score more runs, and teams that score more runs win more games. Yet in 2002, players with high OBP were available at below-market prices. Players like Scott Hatteberg (.374 OBP in 2002) and David Justice (.370 OBP) were affordable because their most valuable skill, i.e., getting on base, wasn’t appreciated sufficiently by the market.
The strategy worked: the 2002 A’s ranked 2nd in the American League (AL) in OBP (.339) despite having the third-lowest payroll in baseball.
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
In 2002, the A’s achieved 4th highest OBP (.349) with 3rd lowest payroll ($40M) [3][4].
Scott Hatteberg is undervalued.
Scott Hatteberg was available at a below-market price due to perceived limitations. The former Boston Red Sox catcher developed nerve damage in his throwing elbow, making catching nearly impossible and leaving him without a clear defensive position.
Oakland signed Hatteberg to first base for $950K on a one-year contract after Colorado declined salary arbitration. The A’s saw past the injury to identify his core value: exceptional plate discipline and on-base skills. His .367 OBP in 2000 and .410 OBP in 1999 demonstrated an ability to get on base that strongly correlated with offensive production.
The position switch to first base was unprecedented; he had never played the position professionally. He learned first base during spring training with infield coach Ron Washington.
Hatteberg’s 2002 performance validated the analytical approach: .280/.374/.433 slash line, 68 walks versus 56 strikeouts, and 4.15 pitches per plate appearance (3rd in AL). His defining moment came on September 4, 2002, when his walk-off home run against Kansas City secured the A’s 20th consecutive victory and set an AL record.
Hatteberg hit a walk-off home run to give the A’s a 12–11 win and a then-AL record 20-game winning streak.
The streak is historic and remarkable.
The 20-game winning streak (August 13 — September 4, 2002) became the dramatic centerpiece of the Moneyball story.
The streak’s climactic finish, Oakland blowing an 11–0 lead to Kansas City before Hatteberg’s walk-off home run, provided Hollywood-worthy drama that helped make the analytical approach culturally compelling.
More importantly, the streak occurred during a season where the A’s won 103 games despite having one of baseball’s lowest payrolls.

Zoom image will be displayed
The A’s achieved 103 wins (tied for MLB lead) with the 3rd lowest payroll

data.title: RE#: High performance derivative-based regular expression matching (2024)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为RE#的正则表达式匹配工具及其理论基础。RE#基于符号衍生，不使用回溯，支持补集、交集和前后查找等操作。理论分析和实验表明，其主要匹配算法具有线性时间复杂度。在多项基准测试中，RE#比最快的Rust正则引擎快71%以上，并在扩展基准测试中大幅超越其他引擎， often by several orders of magnitude。该工具在形式语言与自动机理论领域具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正则表达式匹配语义、布尔操作符的支持及其语义、正则表达式引擎的工业实现历史

不同观点：
• kazinator认为RE#支持的匹配语义是左侧最长匹配（POSIX），而不是左侧贪婪匹配（PCRE）语义。对于如何在回溯引擎中支持扩展的布尔操作符以及其预期语义存在疑问。具体来说，| 操作符在回溯语义中是非交换的，导致一些关键的分配律不再保持匹配语义。例如，A|B|C|D 在回溯引擎中会从左到右依次尝试匹配，如果A匹配成功，则不再尝试B、C、D。kazinator进一步举例说明，在处理"c.r|carp.t"和输入"carpet-odor"时，贪婪匹配会选择较短的匹配"car"，而最长匹配语义则会选择更长的匹配"carpet"。

• 针对上述问题，kazinator指出最长匹配语义符合集合论解释，其中|操作符是可交换的，R1|R2等同于R2|R1，代表R1和R2匹配的字符串的并集。

• 关于正则表达式工业实现的历史，kazinator指出第一个在命令式语言（C#）中使用导数实现标准正则表达式的工业实现是在2019年，但其在2010年已经在TXR中实现了该功能，并提供了具体的提交哈希和日期作为证据。

• omgtehlion提到RE#的源代码库似乎已被删除，并询问是否有人有实际代码的链接。随后自己回答，指出该功能似乎已经部分合并到dotnet本身，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于回溯引擎中|操作符的非交换性及其对匹配结果的影响。kazinator认为这种行为是不合理的，并提倡最长匹配语义。
• 正则表达式匹配语义的具体实现及其对实际应用的影响是另一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 关于正则表达式引擎工业实现的历史，kazinator提供了早期的实现证据，指出了其贡献，并纠正了相关时间线。

Title:

,

View a PDF of the paper titled RE#: High Performance Derivative-Based Regex Matching with Intersection, Complement and Lookarounds, by Ian Erik Varatalu and Margus Veanes and Juhan-Peep Ernits
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a tool and theory RE# for regular expression matching that is built on symbolic derivatives, does not use backtracking, and, in addition to the classical operators, also supports complement, intersection and lookarounds. We develop the theory formally and show that the main matching algorithm has input-linear complexity both in theory as well as experimentally. We apply thorough evaluation on popular benchmarks that show that RE# is over 71% faster than the next fastest regex engine in Rust on the baseline, and outperforms all state-of-the-art engines on extensions of the benchmarks often by several orders of magnitude.

44633024.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为RE#的正则表达式匹配工具及其理论基础。RE#基于符号衍生，不使用回溯，支持补集、交集和前后查找等操作。理论分析和实验表明，其主要匹配算法具有线性时间复杂度。在多项基准测试中，RE#比最快的Rust正则引擎快71%以上，并在扩展基准测试中大幅超越其他引擎， often by several orders of magnitude。该工具在形式语言与自动机理论领域具有重要意义。

data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一种鲜为人知的编程范式——连接式编程（concatenative programming）。作者试图通过撰写教程来推广这一概念，类似于John Hughes的经典文章《Why Functional Programming Matters》。文章首先指出人们对“连接式编程”定义存在分歧，甚至有人认为这一术语没有实际意义。然而，作者认为连接式编程的核心在于使用函数组合而非函数应用，这与应用式编程语言（applicative language）不同。

文章接着解释了连接式编程的基本原理，强调其通过隐式组合函数来简化编程，避免了命名状态和变量处理等问题。相比传统的函数式编程，连接式编程更简单且更“函数式”。作者还通过示例展示了连接式编程的表达方式，如使用后缀表示法来执行操作。文章最后承诺会进一步讲解连接式编程的工作原理、类型系统及其优缺点。

Introduction
There doesn’t
seem to be a good tutorial out there for concatenative programming, so I
figured I’d write one, inspired by the classic “Why Functional
Programming Matters” by John Hughes. With any luck it will get more people interested in the topic, and give me a URL to hand people when they ask what the heck I’m so excited about.
Foremost, there seems to be some disagreement over what the term “concatenative” actually means.
This Stack Overflow answer
by Norman Ramsey even goes so far as to say:
“…it
is not useful to use the word ‘concatenative’ to describe programming
languages. This area appears to be a private playground for
Manfred von Thun
.
There is no real definition of what constitutes a concatenative
language, and there is no mature theory underlying the idea of a
concatenative language.”
This is rather harsh, and,
well, wrong. Not entirely wrong, mind, just rather wrong. But it’s not
surprising that this kind of misinformation gets around, because
concatenative programming isn’t all that well known. (I aim to change
that.)
Concatenative programming is so called because
it uses function
composition
instead of function
application
—a non-concatenative language is thus called
applicative
.
That’s the defining difference, and it’s as “real” a definition as I
need, because, well, it’s the one that people are using. Bang.
Descriptivism.
One of the problems with functional
programming is that the oft-touted advantages—immutability, referential
transparency, mathematical purity, &c.—don’t
immediately
seem
to apply in the real world. The reason “Why Functional Programming
Matters” was necessary in the first place was that functional
programming had been mischaracterised as a paradigm of negatives—no
mutation, no side-effects—so everybody knew what you
couldn’t
do, but few people grasped what you
could
.
There is a similar problem with concatenative programming. Just look at the Wikipedia introduction:
A
concatenative programming language is a point-free programming language
in which all expressions denote functions and the juxtaposition of
expressions denotes function composition. The combination of a
compositional semantics with a syntax that mirrors such a semantics
makes concatenative languages highly amenable to algebraic manipulation.
This is all true—and all irrelevant to your immediate problem of
why you should care
. So in the next sections, I will show you:
How concatenative programming works
How typing in a concatenative language works
How concatenative languages are efficient
What concatenative languages are
not
good for
Where to go for more information
Now let’s get started!
♦ ♦ ♦
The Basics
In
an applicative language, functions are applied to values to get other
values. λ-calculus, the basis of functional languages, formalises
application as “β-reduction”, which just says that if you have a
function (
f
x
=
x
+ 1) then you can substitute a call to that function (
f
y
) with its result (
y
+ 1). In λ-calculus, simple juxtaposition (
f
x
) denotes application, but function composition must be handled with an explicit composition function:
compose := λ
f
. λ
g
. λ
x
.
f
(
g
x
)
This definition says “the composition (compose) of two functions (
f
and
g
) is the result of applying one (
f
) to the result of the other (
g
x
)”,
which is pretty much a literal definition. Note that this function can
only be used to compose functions of a single argument—more on this
later.
In concatenative languages, composition is implicit
: “
f
g
” is the composition of
f
and
g
. However, this does not mean that function application becomes explicit—it actually becomes
unnecessary
. And as it turns out, this peculiar fact makes these languages a whole lot simpler to build, use, and reason about.
The
untyped λ-calculus is a relatively simple system. However, it and the
many systems derived from it still need three kinds of term—variables,
lambdas, and applications—as well as a number of rules about how to
correctly replace variable names when applying functions. You have to
deal with name binding, closures, and scope. For a supposedly low-level
language, it has quite a bit of inherent complexity.
Concatenative languages have a much simpler basis—
there are
only
functions and compositions
, and evaluation is just the
simplification
of functions. It is never necessary to deal with named state—there are
no variables. In a sense, concatenative languages are “more functional”
than traditional functional languages! And yet, as we will see, they are
also easy to implement efficiently.
♦ ♦ ♦
Composition
Let’s say we want to multiply a couple of numbers. In a typical concatenative language, this looks like:
2 3 ×
There are two weird things about this.
First,
we use postfix notation (2 3 ×) rather than the prefix notation (× 2 3)
that is common in the functional world, or the infix notation (2 × 3)
that most languages provide for convenience. There is nothing
stopping
a concatenative language from having infix op

data.title: Superfunctions: A universal solution against sync/async fragmentation in Python
data.author: pomponchik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Python中同步和异步代码分裂的问题，以及一个名为`transfunctions`的库如何通过模板和代码生成来解决这一问题。Python使用`async`和`await`关键字来实现异步编程，导致代码被“染色”，同步和异步函数不能直接互调，导致代码重复。`transfunctions`库通过将一个函数模板转换为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数，从而避免代码重复。该库基于AST（抽象语法树）进行代码生成，允许开发者创建“超级函数”，这些函数可以根据使用方式表现为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数。这样，开发者无需手动区分函数的同步或异步特性，从而简化代码编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中的同步与异步编程模型及其复杂性

不同观点：
• **nilslindemann**：认为当前的异步（async）命名不准确，建议重新定义命名和操作符。他提议一种新的编程方式，通过单个操作符来指定代码的执行顺序，允许并行或异步执行，但在某个点必须汇合（join）以继续执行。他强调当前的命名导致了不必要的复杂性。

• **PaulHoule**：对nilslindemann的提议持怀疑态度，认为其方案会导致编写和使用超级函数（superfunctions）都很 awkward。他提出，异步编程通常需要访问网络、管道或进行睡眠操作，建议将这些上下文封装在对象中，并通过类来实现。他还提到，可以通过包装HTTP API来减少重复代码。

• **operator-name**：认为nilslindemann的方案可能会引入更多功能变体，增加复杂性。他提到asgiref和synchronicity作为现有解决方案，分别通过简单的包装器和100%异步代码暴露同步和异步接口来解决此问题。他担心nilslindemann的方案可能会导致性能问题和理解困难。

• **pomponchik**：支持超级函数的概念，认为它可以减少Python生态系统中同步和异步版本的代码重复，提供客户端选择的机会，类似于Zig语言的实现。

• **RS-232**：认为nilslindemann的方案仍然在模板函数中复制代码，建议装饰器应自动抽象出上下文管理器。他提出I/O绑定操作可以是异步的，而其他操作应该是同步的。

• **rsyring**：对使用波浪号（~）调用函数的语法和机制提出质疑，指出其限制（如无法使用返回值和异常处理）。他认为自己不是该库的目标用户。

• **OutOfHere**：建议放弃Python中的异步编程，因为Python的未来是自由线程的，而异步是单线程的。他认为即使现在不需要多线程，将来也会需要，使用自由线程可以避免完全重写代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效地实现和使用同步与异步编程模型，减少复杂性和代码重复。
• 不同的解决方案包括重新定义命名和操作符、封装对象、使用现有工具如asgiref和synchronicity、以及抽象出超级函数。
• 对异步编程的实用性和未来发展方向存在不同看法，部分人认为异步模型过于复杂且受限，而另一些人则支持通过现有工具和模式来简化问题。

This library is designed to solve one of the most important problems in python programming - dividing all written code into 2 camps: sync and async. We get rid of code duplication by using templates.
Table of contents
Quick start
The problem
Code generation
Markers
Superfunctions
Quick start
Install it:
pip install transfunctions
And use:

asyncio

As you can see, in this case, 3 different functions were created based on the template, including both common parts and unique ones for a specific type of function.
You can also quickly try out this and other packages without having to install using
instld
.
The problem
Since the
asyncio
module appeared in Python more than 10 years ago, many well-known libraries have received their asynchronous alternates. A lot of the code in the Python ecosystem has been
duplicated
, and you probably know many such examples.
The reason for this problem is that the Python community has chosen a way to implement asynchrony expressed through syntax. There are new keywords in the language, such as
async
and
await
. Their use makes the code so-called "
multicolored
": all the functions in it can be red or blue, and depending on the color, the rules for calling them are different. You can only call blue functions from red ones, but not vice versa.
I must say that implementing asynchronous calls using a special syntax is not the only solution. There are languages like Go where runtime can independently determine "under the hood" where a function should be asynchronous and where not, and choose the correct way to call it. A programmer does not need to manually "colorize" their functions there. Personally, I think that choosing a different path is the mistake of the Python community, but that's not what we're discussing here.
The solution offered by this library is based on templating. You can take a certain function as a template and generate several others based on it: regular, asynchronous, or generator. This allows you to avoid duplicating code where it was previously impossible. And all this without major changes in Python syntax or in the internal structure of the interpreter. We're just "sweeping under the carpet" syntax differences. Combined with the idea of context-aware functions, this makes for an even more powerful tool:
superfunctions
. This allows you to create a single function object that can be handled as you like: as a regular function, as an asynchronous function, or as a generator. The function will behave the way you use it. Thus, this library solves the problem of code duplication caused by the syntactic approach to marking asynchronous execution sections.

44634030.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Python中同步和异步代码分裂的问题，以及一个名为`transfunctions`的库如何通过模板和代码生成来解决这一问题。Python使用`async`和`await`关键字来实现异步编程，导致代码被“染色”，同步和异步函数不能直接互调，导致代码重复。`transfunctions`库通过将一个函数模板转换为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数，从而避免代码重复。该库基于AST（抽象语法树）进行代码生成，允许开发者创建“超级函数”，这些函数可以根据使用方式表现为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数。这样，开发者无需手动区分函数的同步或异步特性，从而简化代码编写。
44634030.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中的同步与异步编程模型及其复杂性

不同观点：
• **nilslindemann**：认为当前的异步（async）命名不准确，建议重新定义命名和操作符。他提议一种新的编程方式，通过单个操作符来指定代码的执行顺序，允许并行或异步执行，但在某个点必须汇合（join）以继续执行。他强调当前的命名导致了不必要的复杂性。

• **PaulHoule**：对nilslindemann的提议持怀疑态度，认为其方案会导致编写和使用超级函数（superfunctions）都很 awkward。他提出，异步编程通常需要访问网络、管道或进行睡眠操作，建议将这些上下文封装在对象中，并通过类来实现。他还提到，可以通过包装HTTP API来减少重复代码。

• **operator-name**：认为nilslindemann的方案可能会引入更多功能变体，增加复杂性。他提到asgiref和synchronicity作为现有解决方案，分别通过简单的包装器和100%异步代码暴露同步和异步接口来解决此问题。他担心nilslindemann的方案可能会导致性能问题和理解困难。

• **pomponchik**：支持超级函数的概念，认为它可以减少Python生态系统中同步和异步版本的代码重复，提供客户端选择的机会，类似于Zig语言的实现。

• **RS-232**：认为nilslindemann的方案仍然在模板函数中复制代码，建议装饰器应自动抽象出上下文管理器。他提出I/O绑定操作可以是异步的，而其他操作应该是同步的。

• **rsyring**：对使用波浪号（~）调用函数的语法和机制提出质疑，指出其限制（如无法使用返回值和异常处理）。他认为自己不是该库的目标用户。

• **OutOfHere**：建议放弃Python中的异步编程，因为Python的未来是自由线程的，而异步是单线程的。他认为即使现在不需要多线程，将来也会需要，使用自由线程可以避免完全重写代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效地实现和使用同步与异步编程模型，减少复杂性和代码重复。
• 不同的解决方案包括重新定义命名和操作符、封装对象、使用现有工具如asgiref和synchronicity、以及抽象出超级函数。
• 对异步编程的实用性和未来发展方向存在不同看法，部分人认为异步模型过于复杂且受限，而另一些人则支持通过现有工具和模式来简化问题。

data.title: NixOS on a Tuxedo InfinityBook Pro 14 Gen9 AMD Laptop
data.author: brainlessdev
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者在TUXEDO笔记本上安装和配置NixOS的过程。TUXEDO是一家德国电脑制造商，特别支持Linux系统，预装基于KDE Plasma的TUXEDO OS。由于NixOS并非TUXEDO官方支持的系统，作者需要手动进行一些配置。

主要步骤包括：
1. 启用额外的内核模块以支持Ethernet。
2. 修改内核参数解决笔记本关闭时的唤醒和风扇问题。
3. 使用社区维护的flake来安装TUXEDO Control Center，以管理CPU频率和电源配置文件，而非使用KDE Plasma的PowerDevil。

作者强调了TUXEDO Control Center的一些功能优势，如系统托盘图标和电源配置切换，并提供了相关配置代码示例和问题解决方法。最终，作者成功在TUXEDO InfinityBook Pro 14 Gen9 AMD型号上配置了NixOS。
