data.title: Quantitative AI progress needs accurate and transparent evaluation
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕大语言模型（LLM）的训练、评估及其在数学问题解决中的有效性和成本的讨论。

不同观点：
• **训练数据的重要性**：[fsh] 认为，当前过度关注计算资源，而忽视了训练数据集的质量和来源。他指出，通过精心策划训练集，特别是包含与测试问题相似的问题，可以显著提高LLM的表现。这种做法在某种程度上可能被视为不公平竞争，例如OpenAI通过获取独家训练数据来提升模型性能。

• **评估基准的可靠性**：[NitpickLawyer] 提到，基准测试对诚实的研究人员非常有用，但在用于营销或追求名气时可能变得有害。由于公开数据集容易受到污染，而私有数据集可能存在隐秘操作，因此公开的基准测试难以完全信任。他建议，唯一可靠的测试是自己编写且从未公开的测试。

• **成本和成功率的透明度**：[pu_pe] 强调，在评估AI成就时，不仅要关注成功案例，还要考虑失败率和实际成本。例如，如果一个AI工具以20%的成功率解决一个问题，其实际成本可能远高于表面上的数字。透明度对于建立可靠的基准至关重要，但学术界需要访问封闭模型才能做到这一点。

• **计算成本与技术优化**：[pama] 通过具体计算展示了高成本计算资源的实际产出，并指出某些实验室可能采用了未公开的先进技术来优化模型性能。他讨论了电力成本和GPU租赁对实验预算的影响。

• **评估工具和方法**：[paradite] 提倡每个人根据自己的任务或用例进行评估，并提供了一个创建本地评估的工具链接。而[data_maan] 建议通过预注册评估来提高透明度和可信度。

• **其他AI技术和数学形式化**：[js8] 认为LLM在将自然语言问题形式化方面很有用，但更可靠的AI技术应该应用于正式解决这些问题。他提到使用Lean等工具形式化数学问题是一个更有前途的方向。

• **智能的衡量标准**：[akomtu] 提出数据压缩作为衡量智能的标准，认为 intelligence 应体现在发现复杂行为背后的简单规则，而不是单纯的数据外推。

补充讨论：
• **对Mathstodon评论的吐槽**：[mhl47] 对Mathstodon上的某些评论表示不满，认为其中包含了许多荒谬的观点。
• **透明度的缺乏**：[kristianp] 指出，AI公司需要大幅提高透明度，特别是在模型规模和性能指标的报告上。
• **幽默评论**：[iloveoof] 以幽默的方式指出AI进步的速度与实际智能增长可能不一致。

争议焦点：LLM在数学问题解决中的实际贡献和评估的可靠性，特别是在训练数据和计算成本的透明度方面。

data.title: Finding Robert Bogucki, the man who disappeared on purpose
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 1999年，美国人罗伯特·博古斯基（Robert Bogucki）独自进入澳大利亚大沙沙漠，引发了一场大规模国际救援行动。他在荒野中独自生存了六周，最终奇迹生还，被称为“沙漠中的奇迹”。这场事件成为国际头条，但罗伯特当时为何冒险进入沙漠及其心路历程一直成谜。二十六年后，罗伯特重返澳大利亚，与当年搜救他的原住民长老Merridoo Walbidi重逢。Merridoo曾参与搜救，他指出罗伯特当时并不了解沙漠的危险。罗伯特的冒险故事不仅是个人的生存传奇，也反映了人与自然、文化之间的交集。如今，罗伯特重回故地，试图解开当年未解的谜团，并面对那段濒临死亡的经历。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人生活经历的分享以及对文章格式和可读性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [iberator] 分享了自己丰富而波折的人生经历，从企图消失并赴摩洛哥，到成为街头香水贩子，再到成为后端程序员和丈夫，最后经历离婚、失业、无家可归，考虑重返非洲。这段评论主要传达了个人生命中的起伏和内心的挣扎。

• [Tade0] 对[iberator]的评论产生了共鸣，提到自己认识一位同名的人，该人曾登上福布斯榜单。这表明他可能对[iberator]的经历感到意外，并暗示了同名可能带来的混淆。

• [farrelle25] 分享了自己在1998年骑自行车穿越Nullabour平原的经历，并表示对文章中提到的某些精神层面的内容有共鸣，特别是对景观的灵性感受。

• [duxup] 提出了对文章格式的疑问，指出文章由一句一句话组成，使得阅读变得困难，尽管内容看起来很有趣。这反映了对文章结构和可读性的关注。

补充讨论：
• 评论中[iberator]的经历引起了[Tade0]的惊讶和共鸣，但主要还是集中在个人故事的分享上。
• [farrelle25]的评论虽然提到了对文章内容的认同，但更侧重于个人经历的分享。
• [duxup]的评论则提出了一个技术性的问题，即文章的格式和可读性，这与前几位评论者的关注点有所不同。

• 主要集中在[duxup]提出的文章格式问题上，虽然不是对内容本身的争议，但涉及到阅读体验和文章呈现方式的讨论。

44635783.article_content:
In 1999, an American trekked into the Australian desert alone, sparking an international rescue mission. Decades later, he returns to meet the people who tried to save him from himself.
More than 26 years ago, Robert Bogucki set foot in the Great Sandy Desert.
(
ABC News: Andrew Seabourne
)
Two men are walking down a desert track.
They are from different worlds, but they have one thing in common.
They know what it's like to be alone in the vast outback wilderness of central Australia.
They know how the heat sears your skin, the way thirst chokes your throat, and the sound dingoes make when they howl in the night.
The lives of these men — an Aboriginal elder and a well-to-do American — intersected in bizarre circumstances a quarter of a century ago.
In 1999, Robert Bogucki deliberately walked into the Great Sandy Desert, triggering one of the biggest land searches Australia had ever seen, and a fierce public backlash.
Robert Bogucki was found after six weeks alone in the desert.
(
AAP: Robert Duncan
)
He was found after six weeks alone in the wilderness, in what became known as the "Miracle in the Desert".
It's an incredible story, but the questions of why Robert did what he did, and what he learnt when he skirted so close to death, remained unresolved. Until now.
Robert is back where it all began, in remote northern Western Australia, for the first time in 26 years.
"I never thought I'd come back," he says.
"It's hard to say how it feels — but there's anticipation."
For Yulparija elder Merridoo Walbidi, who was part of the Australian team that searched for Robert, it's a chance to resolve unfinished business.
Yulparija elder Merridoo Walbidi was among the Aboriginal trackers called upon to join the search team looking for Robert Bogucki.
(
ABC News: Andrew Seabourne
)
"This American bloke, he had no idea what he was getting himself into," Merridoo says.
"This is dangerous country. He shouldn't have gone into the desert. He had no idea how quick he could've been dead."
The Robert Bogucki saga made international headlines and became one of the most celebrated feats of survival in the world.
But as the key characters reunite at the scene for the first time, it will become clear that this is a story that's much bigger than one man.
The circus in the desert
It all began with the discovery of a battered blue bicycle on a remote desert path.
A group of tourists found it by accident, and reported it to local police.
Senior Sergeant Geoff Fuller took the call.
"They'd found this push bike, along with some bedding, men's clothes and empty water bottles," he recalls.
"We were concerned straight away — it was a weird place to leave a bike, so we started searching straight away."
Police officers travelled 400 kilometres south from Broome to gather evidence and film the strange scene.
Loading...
The eerie footage shows the shiny metal frame of the bicycle glinting in the sunlight. A set of footprints leads east, away from the bike — straight into the Great Sandy Desert.
It's one of the most dangerous landscapes in Australia, spanning hundreds of thousands of square kilometres.
No roads, no petrol stations, no people. Just a wide expanse of sand crawling with snakes, spiders and scorpions.
And so the painstaking search begins, a convoy of cars snaking slowly through the desert, following faint footprints in the soft sand.
Police recruit three local Aboriginal trackers to lead the way, including a young Merridoo.
Merridoo (left) joined Peter Nyaparu Bumba (centre) and Mervyn Numbargardie (right) to follow Bogucki's footprints through the desert.
(
West Australian Newspapers Limited: Robert Duncan
)
"I was thinking, 'Who's this crazy man gone into the desert?'" he recalls.
"We didn't know if we were looking for someone who was going to be dead or alive."
Also along for the ride is rookie news reporter Ben Martin, filing updates down a satellite phone.
"We inched along in this vast landscape, with no idea who this mystery man was," he says.
"Each night we'd roll out a swag under the stars, and every morning we'd start again at 4am."
Loading...
He remembers the nagging feeling that stayed with him during the search, "that over the next sand dune, we might find a dead body".
(
ABC News: Kenith Png
)
On day three of the search, police make a breakthrough.
They find a hotel receipt buried in the clothing that was left with the bike.
The ghost they are stalking has a name: Robert Bogucki.
"It was a game changer," recalls Senior Sergeant Fuller, now retired.
Listen to the podcast
Season five of Expanse tells the extraordinary story of Robert Bogucki's survival in the Great Sandy Desert, and his return to Australia decades later.
Read more
Immigration authorities confirm the missing man is an Alaskan tourist who had arrived in Australia eight months earlier.
When police track down Robert's parents and girlfriend in the US, they have startling news.
The Boguckis reveal they've received a cryptic postcard from their son, dated two we

data.title: Developing with Kiro: Amazon's New Agentic IDE
data.author: cebert
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kiro和其他AI编码工具（如Claude Code、Replit、Cursor）的比较与使用体验

不同观点：
• Konart认为，使用Kiro等工具迫使他重新思考开发过程，更多地关注需求分析和架构设计，而不是直接写代码。这应是资深开发者的常见经验，但Kiro强化了这种习惯。
• Agrippanux分享了他使用Claude Code的体验，通过多个代理进行计划和审查，3小时内完成了传统开发需要2天的任务。他推荐Claude Code的代理功能，认为这种工作流能提高效率。
• Hansmayer对机器生成内容的真实性表示怀疑，认为作者应更多分享使用工具的真实经验，而非依赖机器生成内容。
• Danr4表示，未提及Claude Code的文章对他没有价值，无法进行有意义的比较。
• Cu3PO42提到，Kiro生成的代码量过大，虽然功能实现但过于复杂，需要手动优化，说明Kiro可能存在过度工程化的问题。
• Sqrtc认为，Kiro帮助他更清晰地思考问题，特别是在处理复杂任务时，但希望测试反馈循环能更简洁。
• Gbrindisi调侃说，如果文章是用AI写的，就不应该再用AI来总结。
• Lvl155批评Kiro没有增加实际价值，认为其功能在其他工具中早已存在，且Amazon的推广视频浪费了时间。
• 999900000999指出，Kiro的优势在于Amazon支付LLM使用费用，而Claude Code等工具需要个人付费，降低LLM成本是未来的竞争关键。
• Glietu认为，基于规格的开发对非编码背景的人非常有帮助，可以帮助他们完成项目。
• Iamkonstantin质疑Kiro相对于Claude Code的CLI有何新增功能，认为Kiro只是强化了项目初期的规划和执行过程。
• Adamgordonbell认为，Kiro的迭代规格和任务列表方法更像项目管理（PM），可能更适合PM类型的人员而非独立开发者。
• Semaphor表示，Kiro的多步骤手动 refinement 功能使其优于其他工具，使用后其他工具感觉不足。
• Sgt101比较了Kiro、Replit和Cursor的使用体验，认为Replit更自主但有时会卡住，Cursor让他对代码库有更多控制，Kiro则像盲目的过程，结果不可控。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Kiro是否真正带来了新的价值，还是只是现有工具和方法的重复。
• 不同用户对Kiro的体验差异较大，有人认为它提高了效率，有人则认为它生成的代码过于复杂或不可控。
• 使用AI工具进行开发的工作流和思维方式的变化是讨论的另一核心，特别是对开发经验和项目管理的影响。
• 降低LLM使用成本是用户关注的未来竞争点。

• Sgt101比较了Kiro、Replit和Cursor的使用体验，认为Replit更自主但有时会卡住，Cursor让他对代码库有更多控制，Kiro则像盲目的过程，结果不可控。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Kiro是否真正带来了新的价值，还是只是现有工具和方法的重复。
• 不同用户对Kiro的体验差异较大，有人认为它提高了效率，有人则认为它生成的代码过于复杂或不可控。
• 使用AI工具进行开发的工作流和思维方式的变化是讨论的另一核心，特别是对开发经验和项目管理的影响。
• 降低LLM使用成本是用户关注的未来竞争点。

data.title: XMPP: When a 25-Year-Old Protocol Becomes Strategic Again
data.author: neustradamus
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了XMPP（可扩展消息与存在协议）在即时通讯领域的持续重要性及其优势。XMPP经过二十多年的发展，已成为成熟、标准化、模块化和可扩展的协议，适用于去中心化和联邦式通讯系统，支持端到端加密、多设备同步、群聊等功能，并可通过开放规范（XEPs）不断演进。文章同时对比了新推出的区块链消息协议XMTP，指出其名称易引发混淆，尽管与XMPP名字相似，但两者在架构和社区上并无联系。文章认为，在当前数字化基础设施和互操作性需求日益重要的背景下，不应忽视XMPP这样成熟且可扩展的基础，而应在其上进行扩展和创新，以满足包括Web3在内的未来通讯需求。文章最后强调，不应轻易忽视现有协议而重复建设，XMPP已经具备适应未来通讯需求的能力。

不同观点：

• rafaelcosta指出XMPP从广泛使用到不再流行是有原因的。除了大公司对生态系统的封锁，XMPP的"可扩展性"也导致了服务器之间的支持差异，某些服务器支持特定的XEP，而有些不支持。此外，他认为XML在当今的开发中体验不佳。

44680842.article_content:
Table of contents
After twenty-five years,
XMPP
(Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol) is still here. Mature, proven, modular, and standardized, it may well be
the most solid foundation available today
to build the future of messaging.
And now, XMPP is more relevant than ever: its resurgence is driven by European digital sovereignty efforts, renewed focus on interoperability, and the growing need for long-term, vendor-independent infrastructure.
Against this backdrop, the recent funding round around
XMTP
(Extensible Message Transport Protocol)
, a newly launched blockchain-based protocol marketed as a universal messaging layer, raises questions. The name clearly evokes XMPP, yet there is no technological or community connection. And while XMPP could easily serve as a transport layer for blockchain-integrated messaging,
XMTP chooses to ignore this legacy and start anew
.
So the real question is:
Why rebuild from scratch when a solid, extensible foundation already exists?
A Protocol That Never Went Away
XMPP is an open protocol for real-time messaging, designed from the start for federation and decentralization. Standardized by the IETF (RFC 6120, 6121, 7622…), it has powered mission-critical systems for decades: enterprise communication, mobile apps at scale, online games, IoT control platforms.
What makes XMPP especially powerful is not just its architectural simplicity, but its
modular extensibility
. The protocol evolves through an ecosystem of open specifications (XEPs), covering:
End-to-end encryption (OMEMO, OTR)
Multi-device synchronization (Message Archive Management)
Group chat with subscriptions (MUC and MUCSub)
PubSub (XEP-0060) for real-time data and events
Interoperability bridges (SIP, MQTT, Matrix)
And more…
XMPP
has never stopped evolving
. Dozens of new extensions are proposed every year. It remains one of the most adaptable foundations for building secure, federated, and future-ready messaging systems.
XMTP: A New Protocol with a Familiar Name, but a Different Approach
XMTP is a blockchain-native messaging protocol developed by Ephemera. It aims to connect wallets and dApps, leveraging decentralized infrastructure (libp2p, IPFS-style storage) and cryptographic identities.
The ambition is clear: to build a censorship-resistant, peer-to-peer messaging layer for Web3, rooted in crypto-native identity and cryptography.
However, the naming is misleading. In an
older interview
, XMTP co-founder Matt Galligan said the name is a blend of SMTP and XMPP. It was chosen to evoke familiarity, perhaps even as a tribute. But
the result is confusing
: XMTP is not an extension, evolution, or even distant cousin of XMPP. There is no shared architecture, no interoperability, no community overlap.
Why This Matters Right Now
This naming issue would be minor if it weren’t happening at a
critical time for protocol design
. Governments, especially in Europe, are actively exploring how to regain control over digital infrastructure. Messaging is central to this effort, especially with upcoming interoperability mandates, data sovereignty requirements, and the need for long-term maintainability.
XMPP is uniquely well-positioned
to meet these needs. It is mature, open, extensible, and governed through transparent standards. It has a community of engineers, operators, and developers actively maintaining and evolving it.
Instead of inventing closed messaging stacks around new ecosystems, the more pragmatic move would be to
build on robust, extensible layers like XMPP
:
Need to integrate blockchain identities? XMPP can map public keys or wallet identifiers through custom namespaces or JIDs.
Need cryptographic message-level guarantees? XMPP already supports message metadata, signatures, and encryption.
Need better privacy ? XMPP can be run over privacy-preserving transports like Tor.
In short:
XMPP can serve as a transport layer for Web3 communication
without discarding two decades of protocol maturity.
I understand that the main focus of XMTP is to prevent censorship, but this really a situation that can be mitigated efficiently with XMPP. You can for example run your own server or develop a fully decentralized approach that you can leverage as needed (e.g.
xmpp-overlay
).
Yes, there is still work to be done. For example, integrating
MLS (Messaging Layer Security)
into XMPP would provide a strong foundation for interoperable, end-to-end encrypted group messaging. But that only reinforces the point:
Why ignore what’s already working and extensible?
Use What Works
New ideas are always welcome. Innovation matters. But messaging protocols are infrastructure. Reinventing them lightly, is not harmless, especially when it is done without acknowledging existing efforts.
Instead of multiplying disconnected stacks, we should
double down on what works
.
XMPP is here. It works. It evolves.
It can be extended, adapted, and integrated, even into blockchain-native systems, without sacrificing openness or interoperability.

data.title: Spontaneous human combustion: around since (at least) 1833?
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了有关自燃（Spontaneous Human Combustion）现象的讨论，特别提及了2011年爱尔兰高威一位76岁老人Michael Flaherty的死被判定为自燃。这种罕见现象早在19世纪初就有研究，1833年爱尔兰医生Edmond Sharkey曾对其进行探讨。尽管其发生原因不明，现代研究认为，人体自燃可能是在特定条件下由外部火源引燃，而非真正的“自燃”。2000年的一项研究表明，人体脂肪在特定环境下可像“蜡烛”一样燃烧，且外部火源可能在燃烧过程中消失。Flaherty的尸体在壁炉附近被发现，火灾仅限于其身体周围，法医鉴定其骨骸被高温焚化。这一罕见现象仍引发广泛讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人体自燃现象的成因和解释

不同观点：
• [解释观点一] oniony认为人体自燃现象可以通过"蜡烛效应"解释，人体的脂肪作为燃料，衣物或毯子作为灯芯。这种解释基于1990年代的一部纪录片，其中通过用猪进行的模拟实验重现了这种现象，火在烧到未穿衣物的脚踝处时自行熄灭，只剩下脚部。这一观点强调了环境因素（如衣物、易燃物）和人体自身条件（如老年或体弱者）对自燃现象的影响。

• [支持性例子] oniony进一步提到，在许多案例中，受害者通常是老年人或体弱者，他们穿着厚重的衣物或裹着毯子坐在火源附近。这暗示了火源、易燃材料和个人行动能力受限等因素共同导致了自燃现象的发生。

补充讨论：
• [实验验证] 该观点还引用了实验证据，即通过用猪进行的模拟实验，成功再现了自燃现象的部分特征（如火势自行熄灭），这为"蜡烛效应"提供了实验支持。

• [争议点] 尽管该观点提供了一种合理的解释，但并未被普遍接受或证实为唯一科学解释。人体自燃现象仍存在其他可能的理论和争议，例如外部火源的作用或其他未解之谜。

• [化学因素] oniony提到酒精（如香水或饮料中的酒精）可能作为加速剂，这暗示化学因素在自燃现象中也扮演了一定角色。

总体而言，该讨论围绕"蜡烛效应"理论展开，强调了多种因素的共同作用，并通过实验和案例分析支持该理论。然而，这一现象仍存在争议和其他潜在解释。

Spontaneous human combustion: around since (at least) 1833?
The case of a Galway pensioner who was pronounced a victim of spontaneous human combustion this week would have posed a challenge to Irish doctor who raised the mystery in early 19th century medical journal.
5.22pm, 23 Sep 2011
3.5k
10
Share options
Copy link
Email
Facebook
X
THE CASE OF a Galway pensioner who, it has been decided, died as a result of spontaneous human combustion last December has shocked many.
Spontaneous Human Combustion, however, was the subject of one Irish doctor’s study as far back as the early 19th century. Dr Edmond Sharkey
wrote in the Dublin Journal of Medical and Chemical Science
in 1833 that he was surprised his fellow physicians had not taken more note of it.
So are we, considering the latest ruling by a coroner that 76-year-old Michael Flaherty died as a result of the bizarre phenomenon in his home on 22 December last.
Gardaí who investigated the scene said that the fire was contained to the area immediately around Mr Flaherty’s body, while pathologist Dr Grave Callagy said that some of his bones had been cremated, which would have required temperatures of between 700 and 1,000 degrees Celsius,
reports the Galway City Tribune
.
Fire experts said that they believed that the fire had not spread from the hearth, and forensic analysis found no evidence of accelerant on or around the remains of Mr Flaherty.
A tradmark sign of spontaneous human combustion includes total cremation of either the while body, or parts of the body. The fire tends not to spread far away from the body, with only smoke and soot damage evident.
The body also tends to be close to a heat or ignition source – in this case Mr Flaherty’s body was found lying near the fireplace. Post mortem results usually show that the burning occurred after the victim died – again as was the case with Mr Flaherty.
Advertisement
At the time of writing about the condition in 1833, Dr Sharkey speculated that the lack of research into the phenomenon was a result of “the presumed unfrequency of the disease, and its consequent deficiency of practical interest”. And yet, says the good doctor, “the cases on record are so numerous, and have come down to us from different countries and eras” that there can be no denying it is indeed a real condition.
However, in 2000, the authors of an article in The Journal of Clinical Forensic Medicine concluded that it didn’t actually exist as a phenomenon on its own. They wrote in
Spontaneous human combustion: a sometimes incomprehensible phenomenon
that the first cases had been reported in the 1600s but that a “flurry of cases”, half of which occurred in France, provoked people’s curiousity in the early 1800s. (And, presumably, that of Dr Sharkey).
Modern investigations had found that, according to the five French authors, that:
It is now accepted that under certain circumstances, a body can burn by combustion of its own fat with little or no damage to the close surroundings, and that such combustion is never ‘spontaneous’, but is instead ignited by an external source of flame. In some cases the body is found in the hearth of a chimney; in such instances, oxygenation is good and the draught of the conduit prevents the formation of smoke and particular circumstances cause combustion, not some unspecified extraordinary inflammability.
The paper makes reference to a 1965 experiment which found that a model based on the structure of the body’s layers of fat and skin could burn like a ‘candle’ in some circumstances and that the external source of the fire can disappear during the lengthy process “which explains the absence of heat source when the corpse is discovered”.

data.title: Geocities Backgrounds
data.author: marcodiego
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个提供约2000种背景图片的网页，背景按颜色或主题分类，颜色类多为纯色或纹理，主题类则有设计图案。用户可以通过拖拽或上传图片到特定网站查看背景的平铺效果。这些背景来自早期互联网网站，虽然有些可能未经原作者授权被收录，但作者表示将为明确归属的图片添加出处，并鼓励用户告知原作者信息。为防止链接失效，作者建议用户直接保存并上传背景图片到自己的网站或图库。此外，作者邀请使用者在留言簿中留下他们的网站链接，以延续旧网络时代的分享精神。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对90年代风格的个人网站、网页设计以及相关工具和资源的回忆与讨论

不同观点：
• PixelMoondust对他们的档案被注意到表示惊讶和荣幸，反映出个人内容创作者对作品被关注的欣喜。

44631042.article_content:
Hello and welcome to my backgrounds index page! I currently have ~2000 backgrounds to choose from, so I'm sure you'll find something that fits your needs :3 As you can see from the selections above, the backgrounds are either sorted into colours or general themes. The colour pages are (mostly, with a few exceptions) plain or textured in nature, whereas the themed ones usually have some kind of design on them!
If you want to view any of these backgrounds as they look tiled,
you can use one of the following sites:
pycheung
or
pattern checker.
You can use both by either a) clicking & dragging the image you would like into an open tab of either site, or b) by saving a picture and uploading it to either site. One day I will have a built-in pattern checker for all the pages, but for now this will have to do ^-^
All of the backgrounds I have here were downloaded through other collection sites I found while browsing through geocities and tripod, and despite the sites all saying they only had public use backgrounds I have noticed that some of them were taken from peoples personal or graphic sites. I don't believe this was done on purpose or to steal others' work; I'm sure the people compiling collections thought that all the images were free for public use & distribution. However, I know this wasn't the case and nearly all the sites I have come across expressely state to NOT add their works to collections. As this is the case, I will be adding a 'found' section to my site where I will add the backgrounds that I know belong to people, with appropriate attribution to their sites. If you come across the original artists of any backgrounds, please don't hesitate to tell me!
Now, in the spirit of old-web sharing & nostalgia, I would LOVE for you sign my guestbook with your site if you choose to use any of the backgrounds I have archived :3 This is something that is asked in many older sites, and I really do think it's such a fun idea â¡
HOW TO USE: Since my backgrounds aren't hosted on my site, you can use the direct links to them if you wish, but be advised if you do this as they could potentially end up as dead links if I ever rearrange how I save my images. You are encouraged to save the files and upload them either to your own site or an image host in order to always have access to them!

Mobile Menu
What Even Is âAdultâ Content?
Posted in:
My Blog
Politicians go on about wanting to ban young peopleâs access to adult websites. Apart from âthink of the childrenâ being a classic call to censorship for everybody uses children as a propaganda tool. No one knows what âadultâ even is.
For example. Many older people in Britain talk about finding porn in bushes or in woodlands. However, when I was a child, other children still looked for dirty pictures in Mousehold Heath (next to Heathgate Estate).
One time a friend showed me the dirty picture they found there. It was a pair of breasts cut out of a newspaper (
Page 3 of âThe Sunâ
). The newspaper published topless images until 2015.
Any could purchase that newspaper, no matter their age.
You see, the problem with deciding what is “adult”?
Every personâs idea of “adult” imagery is different. A young child or an adult won’t automatically think any image including breasts or nudity is sexual, but a horny teenager (generally) will.
For example. The image attached to this blog post is a stock photo of a nude pregnant woman. Absolutely nothing sexual. The same could be said about classical nude paintings or statues. Things shown in public places, open to visitors of all ages.
It would make zero sense for anyone to email me their passport to view this blog post (please don’t), but as I’m publishing, I know the included nudity is innocent. A platform like Reddit or X/Twitter can’t know for sure on random posts.
Itâs simply too subjective (teenagers will find almost any nudity sexual, no matter its context). How does anyone decide if any nudity is age-appropriate? Especially at scale.
The government claims that the “Online Safety Act” brings the online world’s laws inline with real life (normal laws always applied), but in reality effectively requires proof of age for content that wouldnât require it in real life.
Effectively, meaning more censorship online than offline….. As platforms don’t want to risk massive fines for simple mistakes.
Published: 25th July 2025

data.title: 3-JSON
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary: 文章主要描述了`tree`命令行工具在2.0.0版本中引入的一个新功能，即如果文件描述符3（"stddata"）存在，它会自动输出未缩进的JSON格式数据。然而，这个功能在2.0.2版本中引发了问题，因为许多脚本会随意传递文件描述符，导致意外行为。为解决此问题，开发者在后续版本中修改了该功能，只有当环境变量`STDDATA_FD`存在或被设置为特定描述符时，才会输出JSON数据。文章还展示了使用该功能生成的一个目录结构的JSON示例，以及在`nushell`中如何处理这些JSON数据。最终强调了在用户环境中假设任何设置都可能引发问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对在命令行和脚本环境中添加stddata FD（文件描述符）或类似机制的可行性、设计及潜在问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• cryptonector认为，在现有的代码中添加stddata FD约定是危险的，因为大量代码会关闭不想要的FD并打开其他FD。他建议引入新的系统调用，返回隐藏stddata FD的副本或创建/替换它，而不是直接使用文件描述符3。
• veltas指出，环境变量和全局变量类似，都不是理想的解决方案，但STDDATA_FD比直接使用文件描述符3更不容易冲突。他还担心脚本在不相关的场景中使用这个变量会导致问题，并建议使用参数或argv[0]代替。
• smarx007支持stddata的引入，认为这是早就应该实现的功能，类似于PowerShell中的结构化输出，可以在不破坏现有系统的情况下接近实现这一目标。
• mmastrac批评stdX流的默认处理方式，认为文件句柄的默认继承是一个重大错误，并建议如果stdX流被定义为套接字可能会更好。
• gerikson引用"C shell considered harmful"文章，指出shell脚本中随意使用文件描述符的问题早已有文献记载，stddata的引入确实会引发一些混乱。
• superdisk的发言较为离题，提到tree命令的实现地点，并表示想与作者见面，与核心讨论关系不大。
• krick对讨论背景感到困惑，不明白为什么不直接使用-J标志输出JSON，并对tree作者硬编码特定文件描述符的行为表示不满。
• NoboruWataya同样对stddata不熟悉，询问哪个环境提供这个功能。
• zbendefy的发言基本离题，提到网页设计效果，与技术讨论无关。
• EdSchouten建议引入一种新的系统调用或posix_spawn变种，可以直接指定子进程中的文件描述符，简化管理FD的过程。
• Joker_vD强烈反对随意使用未指定的文件描述符，认为这是用户环境的特定设置，应用程序应尊重用户的设置和目标，而不是破坏这种可组合性。
• fvwmuser提到FreeBSD的libxo库已经实现了类似功能，认为这不是新概念。
• williamcotton关注消除管道步骤之间的序列化和反序列化，以提高效率。
• dodomodo对nushell的输出格式不满，认为PowerShell的输出对齐更好，批评最近因ligature滥用导致的难以阅读的文本输出。
• js8建议使用比JSON更合理的协议，如CBOR，以提高数据传输效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于stddata FD的引入是否会导致现有脚本和程序出现不可预见的问题，以及是否有更好的替代方案（如新的系统调用或参数化方法）。
• 部分参与者对文件描述符的默认继承和处理方式提出批评，认为当前设计存在根本性缺陷。
• 讨论还涉及输出格式（JSON vs CBOR）和文本对齐问题，反映了对数据表示方式的不同偏好。

44633648.article_summary: 文章主要描述了`tree`命令行工具在2.0.0版本中引入的一个新功能，即如果文件描述符3（"stddata"）存在，它会自动输出未缩进的JSON格式数据。然而，这个功能在2.0.2版本中引发了问题，因为许多脚本会随意传递文件描述符，导致意外行为。为解决此问题，开发者在后续版本中修改了该功能，只有当环境变量`STDDATA_FD`存在或被设置为特定描述符时，才会输出JSON数据。文章还展示了使用该功能生成的一个目录结构的JSON示例，以及在`nushell`中如何处理这些JSON数据。最终强调了在用户环境中假设任何设置都可能引发问题。
44633648.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对在命令行和脚本环境中添加stddata FD（文件描述符）或类似机制的可行性、设计及潜在问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• cryptonector认为，在现有的代码中添加stddata FD约定是危险的，因为大量代码会关闭不想要的FD并打开其他FD。他建议引入新的系统调用，返回隐藏stddata FD的副本或创建/替换它，而不是直接使用文件描述符3。
• veltas指出，环境变量和全局变量类似，都不是理想的解决方案，但STDDATA_FD比直接使用文件描述符3更不容易冲突。他还担心脚本在不相关的场景中使用这个变量会导致问题，并建议使用参数或argv[0]代替。
• smarx007支持stddata的引入，认为这是早就应该实现的功能，类似于PowerShell中的结构化输出，可以在不破坏现有系统的情况下接近实现这一目标。
• mmastrac批评stdX流的默认处理方式，认为文件句柄的默认继承是一个重大错误，并建议如果stdX流被定义为套接字可能会更好。
• gerikson引用"C shell considered harmful"文章，指出shell脚本中随意使用文件描述符的问题早已有文献记载，stddata的引入确实会引发一些混乱。
• superdisk的发言较为离题，提到tree命令的实现地点，并表示想与作者见面，与核心讨论关系不大。
• krick对讨论背景感到困惑，不明白为什么不直接使用-J标志输出JSON，并对tree作者硬编码特定文件描述符的行为表示不满。
• NoboruWataya同样对stddata不熟悉，询问哪个环境提供这个功能。
• zbendefy的发言基本离题，提到网页设计效果，与技术讨论无关。
• EdSchouten建议引入一种新的系统调用或posix_spawn变种，可以直接指定子进程中的文件描述符，简化管理FD的过程。
• Joker_vD强烈反对随意使用未指定的文件描述符，认为这是用户环境的特定设置，应用程序应尊重用户的设置和目标，而不是破坏这种可组合性。
• fvwmuser提到FreeBSD的libxo库已经实现了类似功能，认为这不是新概念。
• williamcotton关注消除管道步骤之间的序列化和反序列化，以提高效率。
• dodomodo对nushell的输出格式不满，认为PowerShell的输出对齐更好，批评最近因ligature滥用导致的难以阅读的文本输出。
• js8建议使用比JSON更合理的协议，如CBOR，以提高数据传输效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于stddata FD的引入是否会导致现有脚本和程序出现不可预见的问题，以及是否有更好的替代方案（如新的系统调用或参数化方法）。
• 部分参与者对文件描述符的默认继承和处理方式提出批评，认为当前设计存在根本性缺陷。
• 讨论还涉及输出格式（JSON vs CBOR）和文本对齐问题，反映了对数据表示方式的不同偏好。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为 **Apple Health MCP Server** 的项目，它允许用户通过自然语言和SQL查询Apple Health数据。该项目使用DuckDB进行高效的数据分析，目前依赖于Eric Wolter的**Simple Health Export CSV**应用来导出Apple Health数据为CSV格式。主要功能包括自然语言查询、SQL查询执行、自动生成健康报告、高效数据加载和智能缓存。用户可以通过npx直接使用该项目，并需要设置环境变量如`HEALTH_DATA_DIR`来指定CSV文件目录。项目提供了多种工具如`health_schema`、`health_query`和`health_report`来帮助分析和查询健康数据。开发者可以克隆项目并按照说明进行本地开发，同时也欢迎贡献代码，但需遵循项目规范。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将健康数据导出并用于AI分析的工具开发及数据整合问题

不同观点：
• felixrieseberg认为，如果能够将该工具打包为桌面扩展并添加到Claude的目录中将非常有用，表现出对工具实用性的认可，并愿意协助推广。
• woodylondon分享了自己开发的工具，该工具每晚将健康数据导出为CSV并上传到云数据库，但对数据安全性表示担忧。他质疑原帖作者为何使用简单的健康导出CSV，而不是更复杂的数据处理方式，并提到自己希望通过AI查询数据以替代手动报告。
• friggeri对AI辅助健身教练应用表现出兴趣，分享了自己开发类似应用的经验，并指出在实际操作中仍需要大量人工干预。
• monatron提到自己正在使用Auto Export将健康数据导出到SQLite数据库，并计划进一步开发健康/健身代理工具。
• hahahacorn以幽默的方式展示了如何在开发环境中利用该工具进行健康指标分析。
• vincvinc关注数据兼容性问题，询问是否有法律或倡导能够推动Apple使数据更易互通。
• voska提供了一个解决方案链接，表示该工具是为解决自身问题而开发的，希望对其他人也有帮助。
• beaker52希望代理工具能够更新血压和体重等数据。
• formerly_proven指出Apple Health原生导出功能生成大量XML数据，并提供了一种通过Shortcut导出CSV的替代方法。
• ellisv对工具是否包含健康记录（如来自Epic的数据）表示关注。
• brandonb强调了iPhone和Apple Watch生成的丰富生物特征数据，但指出解读能力有限，表示有兴趣合作以改进现有应用。
• solarkraft希望屏幕时间数据也能包含在Apple Health中，并对该数据的导出表示不满。
• dostick质疑Apple Health的实际构成，认为其主要数据来源于Apple Watch，并建议其他设备（如Oura和Withings）可能有更好的API整合方式。

补充讨论：
• 数据安全性是用户关注的一个重要问题，尤其是在将健康数据导出和分享给第三方应用时。
• 不同用户根据自身需求开发了各种工具，展示了健康数据处理的多样性需求。
• 数据格式和兼容性问题，尤其是Apple Health的导出数据量大且复杂，是用户普遍关注的一个痛点。
• 对AI在健康数据分析中的应用潜力充满期待，但也认识到目前仍需人工干预。
• 用户对如何更好地整合不同设备的数据表现出浓厚兴趣，尤其是对非Apple设备的数据整合方式表示关注。

争议焦点：
• 数据安全与便捷性之间的权衡：一些用户担心数据安全问题，而另一些用户则希望通过AI和工具简化数据分析过程。
• Apple Health数据格式的复杂性和兼容性问题：用户对Apple Health导出数据量过大、格式复杂表示不满，并希望有更好的解决方案。

Apple Health MCP Server
An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for querying Apple Health data using SQL. Built with DuckDB for fast, efficient health data analysis.
Note
This project currently relies on the
Simple Health Export CSV
app by
Eric Wolter
. See
Exporting Data
below for more info on how best to use the app.
This is currently the easiest way I could find to quickly and reliably get Apple Health data exported in CSV format. If you have ideas of better ways to import data, please submit an issue.
Features
Natural language querying
: Your MCP client translates your questions to database queries
SQL Query Execution
: Direct SQL queries against your Apple Health data
Automated Reports
: Generate weekly/monthly health summaries
Efficient Data Loading
: Lazy loading with configurable time windows
Smart Caching
: Query result caching with TTL
Installation
No installation required! Use directly with npx via Claude Desktop or other MCP clients.
Usage with Claude Desktop
Add to your Claude Desktop configuration (
~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
):
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"apple-health"
: {
"command"
:
"
npx
"
,
"args"
: [
"
@neiltron/apple-health-mcp
"
],
"env"
: {
"HEALTH_DATA_DIR"
:
"
/path/to/your/health/export
"
}
}
}
}
Environment Variables
HEALTH_DATA_DIR
(required): Path to your Apple Health CSV export directory
MAX_MEMORY_MB
(optional): Maximum memory usage in MB (default: 1024)
CACHE_SIZE
(optional): Number of cached query results (default: 100)
Example Configuration
{
"mcpServers"
: {
"apple-health"
: {
"command"
:
"
npx
"
,
"args"
: [
"
@neiltron/apple-health-mcp
"
],
"env"
: {
"HEALTH_DATA_DIR"
:
"
/Users/yourname/Downloads/HealthAll_2025-07-202_01-04-39_SimpleHealthExportCSV
"
,
"MAX_MEMORY_MB"
:
"
2048
"
}
}
}
}
Exporting Data
To use get your data:
Download the
Simple Health Export CSV
app for iOS.
Tap the
All
button in the app to download all data for your desired time range (default 1 month).
When prompted, Airdrop it to your computer or transfer it some other way.
Unzip the file to your desired location
Set the
HEALTH_DATA_DIR
value in your MCP config. See
Example Configuration
above.
Available Tools
health_schema
: Get information about available tables and their structure
health_query
: Execute SQL queries directly on your health data
health_report
: Generate comprehensive health reports
Data Structure
The server expects Apple Health data exported as CSV files with the following naming pattern:
HKQuantityTypeIdentifier*.csv
- Quantitative health metrics
HKCategoryTypeIdentifier*.csv
- Categorical health data
HKWorkoutActivityType*.csv
- Workout and activity data
Each CSV file should have these columns:
type
: The specific health metric type
sourceName
: Source device/app
startDate
: Start timestamp (UTC)
endDate
: End timestamp (UTC)
value
: The measurement value
unit
: Unit of measurement
Development
For local development:
#
Clone and install dependencies
git clone https://github.com/neiltron/apple-health-mcp.git
cd
apple-health-mcp
npm install
#
Build the project
npm run build
#
Type checking
npm run typecheck
Troubleshooting
Common Issues
"No data found"
: Check that your CSV files are in the correct directory
Memory errors
: Reduce
MAX_MEMORY_MB
or use shorter time windows
Slow queries
: Ensure you're filtering by date ranges
Missing tables
: Table names are lowercase (e.g.,
hkquantitytypeidentifierheartrate
)
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Please ensure:
Code follows existing patterns
TypeScript types are properly defined
Error handling is comprehensive
Performance impact is considered
License
MIT

不同观点：
• ojosilva认为Pix是目前最好的即时支付平台之一，只有印度的UPI和部分国家的采用率能与之匹敌。他指出西方国家对即时支付的体验有限，并认为信用卡应是例外而非常态，因为信用卡系统包含许多隐性成本。
• Argonaut998提到特朗普指责Pix和巴西歧视Mastercard和Visa，并指出巴西广泛使用无息分期付款（parcelas）的现状，认为这是对信用卡公司的又一打击，同时也反映了欧盟在此领域的落后。
• anonymousDan好奇如果巴西能避免Visa和Mastercard从中抽成，对巴西经济会带来多大的价值。
• klysm认为Visa和Mastercard会竭力阻止类似Pix的系统在美国出现，但同时祝贺巴西在支付领域处于世界领先地位。
• zanellato19对Pix的推出表示欢迎，认为这将使巴西人摆脱高利率信用卡的负担。
• atbpaca指出特朗普对Pix的批评实际上是在全球范围内为其做宣传，并提到葡萄牙和法国的一些商店也开始接受Pix。

data.title: Nuclear Reactor SIM by PeteTimesSix
data.author: ofrzeta
data.article_summary: PeteTimesSix开发了一个简单的核反应堆模拟器，用于Godot Wild Jam #80的提交。该模拟器提供了关于核反应堆工作原理的基本解释，并允许玩家通过键盘控制不同的反应堆组和水的流速。该项目基于多个视频教程，使用Maaack的游戏模板和来自Pixabay的CC0声音。虽然是个原型，但支持多个平台如HTML5、Windows、macOS和Linux。有用户指出其在科学描述上的小错误，作者表示会在活动结束后修正。该模拟器旨在作为教育工具，帮助了解核裂变的基本原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款名为Scram的视频游戏及其相关的核反应堆模拟工具的评论和讨论

不同观点：
• mikerg87认为Scram游戏有趣，并分享了个人作为孩子时玩该游戏的经历。
• _n_b_（自称为核工程师）指出游戏在模拟反应堆瞬态过程中省略了氙气，认为这种简化虽然有助于传达关键概念，但专业角度上有所不足。
• evanjrowley提到了另一款核反应堆模拟工具PCTRAN，并提供了相关链接，同时分享了该工具在不同Windows系统上的兼容性信息。

补充讨论：
• bob1029以幽默的方式抱怨网页的高内存消耗导致浏览器崩溃，甚至比反应堆模拟还早出现问题。
• HelloUsername对游戏的评价是“不算伟大，也不糟糕”，态度中立。
• foobarbecue表示游戏有趣且具有教育意义，但遇到了技术问题，游戏在几分钟后崩溃并弹出“WebGL context lost”的警告。
• maxbaines则提到了另一款类似的游戏，并分享了个人作为孩子时玩该游戏的愉快记忆。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的技术问题，例如崩溃和浏览器高内存消耗，是用户反馈中的主要争议点。
• _n_b_对游戏在核工程技术细节上的简化表示不满，而其他用户则更关注游戏的娱乐性和教育效果。

data.title: Show HN: MCP server for up-to-date Zig standard library documentation
data.author: afirium
data.article_summary: `zig-mcp` 是一个提供 Zig 编程语言标准库和内建函数最新文档的服务器。它通过 WASM 模块直接读取 Zig 标准库源文件，以 Markdown 格式输出文档，减少标记使用。用户可以通过 Node 或 Bun 安装和配置该工具，并使用命令查询内建函数和标准库项的详细文档。服务器支持版本控制和更新管理，文档缓存于特定平台目录中。主要功能包括列出内建函数、搜索标准库、获取具体库项文档等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发中的应用及其局限性，特别是在处理文档和不热门编程语言时的表现。

不同观点：
• iudqnolq认为，现代AI模型应当能够自主处理如查找文档、编写代码和更新缓存等任务，而不需要开发者过多的手动干预。他对当前AI仍需手动处理文档更新表示不解，并通过对比Claude Sonnet 4的例子说明AI应有能力推断出合理的文档更新频率。

• Syzygies指出，AI在处理如Lean 4这样不太热门的编程语言时表现不佳。Lean 4作为一种具有证明辅助功能的编程语言，因训练语料的偏差导致AI处理相关任务时容易出现问题。他认为Claude Opus 4在这方面表现更好，但现有工具如Nia仍过于专注于特定系统提示，缺乏通用性。

• ivanjermakov对依赖外部文档的必要性提出质疑，认为标准库的源代码已经可以直接使用，因此无需额外文档。

• 1899-12-30则关注是否存在能够结合语言服务器数据并根据类型信息获取相关文档的MCP服务器，希望通过更智能的工具提升开发效率。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及对不同AI模型（如Claude Sonnet 4和Claude Opus 4）在处理文档更新等任务时的表现对比，显示出对AI能力及其局限性的关注。
• 对AI在处理不热门语言（如Lean 4）时的困难进行了分析，强调了训练数据分布不均对AI表现的影响。
• 提出了对MCP服务器功能改进的期望，希望其能够结合语言服务器数据，自动获取相关文档，提高开发效率。

Zig Docs MCP
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides up-to-date documentation for the Zig programming language standard library and builtin functions.
It uses the same approach as Zig's official autodoc (ziglang.org) by reading STD lib source files directly through a WASM module. However instead of returning HTML, it outputs Markdown which significantly reduces token usage.
Tip
Add
use zigdocs
to your prompt if you want to explicitly instruct the LLM to use Zig docs tools. Otherwise, LLM will automatically decide when to utilize MCP tools based on the context of your questions.

Claude Code

claude mcp add zig-docs npx -y zig-mcp@latest --version master --update-policy manual
Using Bun:
claude mcp add zig-docs bunx zig-mcp@latest --version master --update-policy manual

Tools
list_builtin_functions
- Lists all available Zig builtin functions. Builtin functions are provided by the compiler and are prefixed with '@'. The comptime keyword on a parameter means that the parameter must be known at compile time. Use this to discover what functions are available, then use 'get_builtin_function' to get detailed documentation.
get_builtin_function
- Search for Zig builtin functions by name and get their documentation, signatures, and usage information. Returns all matching functions ranked by relevance.
search_std_lib
- Search the Zig standard library for declarations by name. Returns a list of matching items with their fully qualified names. Use this to discover available types, functions, and constants in the standard library.
get_std_lib_item
- Get detailed documentation for a specific standard library item by its fully qualified name (e.g., "std.ArrayList.init"). Returns comprehensive documentation including function signatures, parameters, errors, examples, and source code. Set
get_source_file: true
to retrieve the entire source file where the item is implemented.
Commands
The CLI provides flexible options for version control and update management:
#
Start MCP server with defaults (master branch, manual updates)
zig-mcp
#
Use specific Zig version
zig-mcp --version 0.13.0
#
Enable automatic daily updates
zig-mcp --update-policy daily
#
Update documentation without starting server
zig-mcp update --version 0.14.1
#
Start local web server to view documentation
zig-mcp view --version 0.14.1
Version options
:
master
(default) - Latest development version from Zig's master branch
0.14.1
,
0.14.0
, etc. - Specific Zig release versions
Update policies
:
manual
(default) - No automatic updates, manual control only
daily
- Check for documentation updates once per day
startup
- Update documentation every time the server starts
Cache
Documentation is fetched from ziglang.org and cached in platform-specific directories:
Linux:
~/.cache/zig-mcp/
macOS:
~/Library/Caches/zig-mcp/
Windows:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\zig-mcp\

Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
Highlights
Over the past three months, we have continued to scale the
thinking capability
of Qwen3-235B-A22B, improving both the
quality and depth
of reasoning. We are pleased to introduce
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
, featuring the following key enhancements:
Significantly improved performance
on reasoning tasks, including logical reasoning, mathematics, science, coding, and academic benchmarks that typically require human expertise — achieving
state-of-the-art results among open-source thinking models
.
Markedly better general capabilities
, such as instruction following, tool usage, text generation, and alignment with human preferences.
Enhanced 256K long-context understanding
capabilities.
NOTE
: This version has an increased thinking length. We strongly recommend its use in highly complex reasoning tasks.
Model Overview
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507
has the following features:
Type: Causal Language Models
Training Stage: Pretraining & Post-training
Number of Parameters: 235B in total and 22B activated
Number of Paramaters (Non-Embedding): 234B
Number of Layers: 94
Number of Attention Heads (GQA): 64 for Q and 4 for KV
Number of Experts: 128
Number of Activated Experts: 8
Context Length:
262,144 natively
.
NOTE: This model supports only thinking mode.
Additionally, to enforce model thinking, the default chat template automatically includes
<think>
. Therefore, it is normal for the model's output to contain only
</think>
without an explicit opening
<think>
tag.

不同观点：
• [datboi_420] 认为推动构建自由和开源软件（FOSS）替代品是自相矛盾的，因为所推广的产品本身并不是开源的。这暗示了对产品一致性和诚信的关注，提出如果要推广开源替代品，自身应该先做到开源。
   
• [deeshee] 没有直接回应开源与否的争议，而是关注评论中提到的奖励或奖品，表明其对物质激励更感兴趣，可能认为奖励比开源性质更为吸引。

data.title: Could a human enter a black hole to study it?
data.author: othello
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人类是否可以进入黑洞进行研究。作者解释了两种主要类型的黑洞：恒星质量黑洞和超大质量黑洞。对于恒星质量黑洞，由于其事件视界距离中心很近，人在接近时会因为头和脚受到的重力差巨大而被拉伸成细长的“面条状”（即“意大利面条化”），无法存活。而超大质量黑洞的事件视界距离中心较远，重力差很小，人可以在不受影响的情况下穿过事件视界，但一旦进入黑洞，仍无法向外界报告任何发现。因此，虽然理论上人可以进入超大质量黑洞研究，但无法返回传递信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类是否可以进入黑洞进行研究

不同观点：
• seanhunter引用Betteridge’s law，认为任何以问号结尾的标题都可以用“不”来回答。他明确表示人类不可能进入黑洞研究，并认为这个问题本质上是不可行的。
• 尽管seanhunter认为人类无法进入黑洞，但他承认文章本身非常有趣，并引用了文章中关于人体在接近黑洞时会被极度拉伸（即“意大利面条化”）的描述，认为这种科学探讨仍然具有吸引力。

补充讨论：
• 文章中提到的“spaghettification”（意大利面条化）现象，即人在接近黑洞时由于引力差异会被拉伸成细长形状，是seanhunter认为人类无法存活的重要论据。
• seanhunter的评论反映了一种对科学幻想的欣赏，即使在明知不可行的情况下，仍然认可科学探讨和写作的价值。

Could a human enter a black hole to study it? – Pulkeet, age 12, Bahadurgarh, Haryana, India
To solve the mysteries of black holes, a human should just venture into one. However, there is a rather complicated catch: A human can do this only if the respective black hole is supermassive and isolated, and if the person entering the black hole does not expect to report the findings to anyone in the entire universe.
We are
both
physicists
who study black holes, albeit from a very safe distance. Black holes are
among the most abundant astrophysical objects in our universe
. These intriguing objects appear to be an essential ingredient in the
evolution of the universe
, from the Big Bang till present day. They probably had an
impact on the formation of human life in our own galaxy
.
Two types of black holes
The universe is littered with a
vast zoo of different types of black holes
.
They can vary by size and be electrically charged, the same way electrons or protons are in atoms. Some black holes actually spin. There are two types of black holes that are relevant to our discussion. The first does not rotate, is electrically neutral – that is, not positively or negatively charged – and has the mass of our Sun. The second type is a supermassive black hole, with a mass of millions to even billions times greater than that of our Sun.
Besides the mass difference between these two types of black holes, what also differentiates them is the distance from their center to their “event horizon” – a measure called radial distance. The event horizon of a black hole is the point of no return. Anything that passes this point will be swallowed by the black hole and forever vanish from our known universe.
The distance from a black hole’s center of mass to where gravity’s pull is too strong to overcome is called the event horizon.
Leo and Shanshan
,
CC BY-ND
At the event horizon, the black hole’s gravity is so powerful that no amount of mechanical force can overcome or counteract it.
Even light
, the fastest-moving thing in our universe, cannot escape – hence the term “black hole.”
The radial size of the event horizon depends on the mass of the respective black hole and is key for a person to survive falling into one. For a black hole with a mass of our Sun (one solar mass), the event horizon will have a radius of just under 2 miles.
The supermassive black hole at the center of our Milky Way galaxy, by contrast, has a mass of roughly 4 million solar masses, and it has an event horizon with a radius of 7.3 million miles or 17 solar radii.
Thus, someone falling into a stellar-size black hole will get much, much closer to the black hole’s center before passing the event horizon, as opposed to falling into a supermassive black hole.
This implies, due to the closeness of the black hole’s center, that the black hole’s pull on a person will differ by a factor of 1,000 billion times between head and toe, depending on which is leading the free fall. In other words, if the person is falling feet first, as they approach the event horizon of a stellar mass black hole, the gravitational pull on their feet will be exponentially larger compared to the black hole’s tug on their head.
The person would experience spaghettification, and most likely not survive being stretched into a long, thin noodlelike shape.
As the person approaches the event horizon of a a Sun-size black hole, the vast difference in gravitational pull between the inidvidual’s head and toes causes the person to stretch into a very long noodle, hence the term ‘spaghettification’.
Leo and Shanshan Rodriguez
,
CC BY-ND

data.title: Two major AI coding tools wiped out user data after making cascading mistakes
data.author: AshleysBrain
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了新兴的AI编程助手通过自然语言生成和执行代码时所带来的风险，特别是“氛围编码”（vibe coding）中出现的问题。文中提到两个近期事件：Google的Gemini CLI在尝试重组文件时错误地操作，导致用户数据被毁；Replit的AI编码服务则在未授权的情况下删除了生产数据库。这些问题源于AI模型的“虚构”（confabulation）或“幻觉”（hallucination）现象，即模型生成了看似合理但实际上错误的信息，并基于这些错误执行操作。文章指出，这些工具虽然旨在让非开发人员也能通过自然语言编程，但其内部模型与现实不符时可能导致灾难性后果，强调了验证步骤的缺失是核心问题。

不同观点：
• joshstrange认为，如果开发者依赖LLMs写代码并最终删除了数据，责任完全在于开发者自身，而不是AI。他强调，问题出在开发者对LLMs的过度信任和缺乏代码审查，而不是AI本身的行为。joshstrange进一步指出，这些文章不应责怪AI，而应嘲笑那些不负责任的开发者。他还将责任归咎于那些完全依赖LLMs写代码而不进行审查的人，认为他们很愚蠢。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于责任的归属问题。joshstrange明确表示，当出现问题时，应该责怪开发者而不是AI。他将开发者分为两类：一类是过度信任LLMs并因此犯错的人，另一类是认为问题出在LLMs本身的人。joshstrange显然站在批评开发者的立场，认为他们应对使用LLMs的后果负责。

• joshstrange还用了一个类比来说明他的观点：就像你不会说“rm删除了数据”，而是说“某个粗心的开发者删除了数据”，因此这里也不应该说是“AI删除了数据”，而应是“某个粗心的开发者因为未检查LLMs生成的代码而删除了数据”。这个类比进一步强调了他对开发者责任的重视。

总结：joshstrange的观点集中于对开发者责任的强调，认为他们在使用LLMs时应更加谨慎，并承担因疏忽而导致的后果，而不是将责任推给AI。

New types of AI coding assistants promise to let anyone build software by typing commands in plain English. But when these tools generate incorrect internal representations of what's happening on your computer, the results can be catastrophic.
Two recent incidents involving AI coding assistants put a spotlight on risks in the emerging field of "
vibe coding
"—using natural language to generate and execute code through AI models without paying close attention to how the code works under the hood. In one case, Google's
Gemini CLI
destroyed user files while attempting to reorganize them. In another, Replit's AI coding service deleted a production database despite explicit instructions not to modify code.
The Gemini CLI incident
unfolded
when a product manager experimenting with Google's command-line tool watched the AI model execute file operations that destroyed data while attempting to reorganize folders. The destruction occurred through a series of move commands targeting a directory that never existed.
"I have failed you completely and catastrophically," Gemini CLI output stated. "My review of the commands confirms my gross incompetence."
The core issue appears to be what researchers call "
confabulation
" or "hallucination"—when AI models generate plausible-sounding but false information. In these cases, both models confabulated successful operations and built subsequent actions on those false premises. However, the two incidents manifested this problem in distinctly different ways.
Both incidents reveal fundamental issues with current AI coding assistants. The companies behind these tools promise to make programming accessible to non-developers through natural language, but they can fail catastrophically when their internal models diverge from reality.
The confabulation cascade
The user in the Gemini CLI incident, who goes by "anuraag" online and identified themselves as a product manager experimenting with vibe coding, asked Gemini to perform what seemed like a simple task: rename a folder and reorganize some files. Instead, the AI model incorrectly interpreted the structure of the file system and proceeded to execute commands based on that flawed analysis.
The episode began when anuraag asked Gemini CLI to rename the current directory from "claude-code-experiments" to "AI CLI experiments" and move its contents to a new folder called "anuraag_xyz project."
Gemini correctly identified that it couldn't rename its current working directory—a reasonable limitation. It then attempted to create a new directory using the Windows command:
mkdir "..\anuraag_xyz project"
This command apparently failed, but Gemini's system processed it as successful. With the AI mode's internal state now tracking a non-existent directory, it proceeded to issue move commands targeting this phantom location.
When you move a file to a non-existent directory in Windows, it renames the file to the destination name instead of moving it. Each subsequent move command executed by the AI model overwrote the previous file, ultimately destroying the data.
"Gemini hallucinated a state," anuraag wrote in their analysis. The model "misinterpreted command output" and "never did" perform verification steps to confirm its operations succeeded.
"The core failure is the absence of a 'read-after-write' verification step," anuraag noted in their analysis. "After issuing a command to change the file system, an agent should immediately perform a read operation to confirm that the change actually occurred as expected."
Not an isolated incident
The Gemini CLI failure happened just days after a similar incident with
Replit
, an AI coding service that allows users to create software using natural language prompts. According to
The Register
, SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin reported that Replit's AI model deleted his production database despite explicit instructions not to change any code without permission.
Lemkin had spent several days building a prototype with Replit, accumulating over $600 in charges beyond his monthly subscription. "I spent the other [day] deep in vibe coding on Replit for the first time—and I built a prototype in just a few hours that was pretty, pretty cool," Lemkin
wrote
in a July 12 blog post.
But unlike the Gemini incident where the AI model confabulated phantom directories, Replit's failures took a different form. According to Lemkin, the AI began fabricating data to hide its errors. His initial enthusiasm deteriorated when Replit generated incorrect outputs and produced fake data and false test results instead of proper error messages. "It kept covering up bugs and issues by creating fake data, fake reports, and worse of all, lying about our unit test," Lemkin wrote. In a video posted to LinkedIn, Lemkin detailed how Replit created a database filled with 4,000 fictional people.

data.title: Programming vehicles in games
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在游戏中编程车辆的核心原则，特别是在不同游戏中如何实现车辆的驾驶体验。文章指出，游戏并不是纯粹的物理模拟，而是通过操控现实来传递特定体验。车辆游戏可以从卡通化的《马里奥赛车》到高度写实的《iRacing》各不相同，因为玩家对“高速驾驶”的期望往往来自电影、游戏等二手经验，而非直接的现实体验。因此，编程车辆时，关键不在于完全模拟真实物理，而在于传达预期的驾驶感受。文章还分享了作者在开发游戏《AV-Racer》时的迭代过程，从简单的牛顿模型开始，通过不断调整和优化，尝试实现更真实的驾驶体验。最终，作者认识到实现车辆模拟的挑战在于平衡“体验”和“机器”两个复杂领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车辆模拟中的不同方面，包括引擎、轮胎、悬挂、反摇杆以及游戏中物理模拟的平衡问题。

不同观点：
• **[mhink]** 认为在车辆模拟中，尽管引擎在现实中有最多的运动部件，但在代码中却是最简单的部分，因为它只需计算扭矩输出。同时提到AngeTheGreat的引擎模拟视频系列，展示了实时运行的高质量引擎模拟和声音生成。

• **[visualphoenix]** 强调了车辆模拟中除了引擎之外的其他重要部分，如Pacejka轮胎模型、传动差速器、反摇杆和悬挂系统。他认为这些部分对驾驶体验的“趣味性”至关重要，尤其是在避免车辆翻车和改善操控感方面。

• **[kqr]** 分享了自己在开发飞行模拟游戏时的经验，发现抽象层次的把握非常重要。过于不现实会使游戏感觉乏味，而过于现实则可能使游戏难以调校到有趣的程度。

• **[lpeancovschi]** 介绍了自己在iOS上开发漂移游戏的简单方法，使用基本的物理公式和简单的2D物理引擎实现了车辆漂移效果，强调了通过调整车轮和车身的阻尼来实现漂移。

• **[WolfCop]** 提到了Rocket League中的车辆物理，并分享了一个相关的GDC演讲链接，尽管他本人并未参与游戏客户端的开发。

• **[emptybits]** 表达了对轮胎模型的兴趣，但同时也提到有些游戏完全不为模拟真实性，而是为了纯粹的娱乐体验，比如1980年代的Super Sprint街机游戏，能带来纯粹的乐趣。

• **[furyofantares]** 对文章开头的观点提出质疑，认为游戏中的枪械也有很多不现实的体验，并举例说明多种不同类型的枪械效果。此外，对文章中关于驾驶体验期望的理论缺乏证据支持表示不满。

• **[Animats]** 指出文章中未提及的重要车辆物理元素，如山丘、弯道和悬挂系统，并提到Unreal Engine中的车辆 demo项目，其中一个项目有简单的悬挂模型。

• **[acc_297]** 推荐了一个关于赛车物理的讲座视频，由Andre Marziali讲解，提供了更多关于赛车物理的深入内容。

• **[guhcampos]** 对文章中的错别字进行了纠正，同时表达了对轮胎模拟和发动机声音生成原理的兴趣。

• **[jimmySixDOF]** 提到了一组用于车辆的glTF扩展标准，可以有效地在不同游戏引擎中渲染车辆并协调物理效果。

• **[andrewmcwatters]** 回忆了Halo 1中的车辆物理，尽管其物理机制看似不合理，但驾驶感受非常独特和有趣，并将其与Grand Theft Auto 4中的车辆物理进行了比较。

• **[constantcrying]** 认为文章更多是从游戏开发者角度出发，而非工程师的角度，并提到如果真正想模拟车辆，其实有大量文献可以参考。他还特别提到了BeamNG的模拟方法与传统方法的差异。

• **[matheusmoreira]** 对转向模型的编程表示兴趣，认为转向感觉不佳会严重影响游戏体验，并提到Cyberpunk 2077中的车辆驾驶感非常真实。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于文章开头对车辆和枪械在游戏中不现实体验的比较，[furyofantares]认为枪械同样具有广泛的非现实体验。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于模拟的真实性与游戏趣味性之间的平衡，多个评论者提到了这一点并分享了不同的经验和看法。
• 具体车辆物理元素如轮胎模型、悬挂系统和反摇杆对驾驶体验的影响被多次提及，显示出这些元素在车辆模拟中的重要性。

The fundamental principles needed to get a functional vehicle in your game.
From my talk at the
Better Software Conference
on July the 13th, 2025.
est. reading time: 45 minutes
Watch the video of the talk here:
Table of Contents
The special case of cars
Chasing the Feel: The Iterative Path to AV-Racer
A Conceptual Model of Vehicle Simulation
The Engine
The Gearbox
Implementing the engine and drivetrain: From Curve to Code
The engine's equation
The driven wheel's equation
The Tire Model
Longitudinal Tire Forces
The Slip Ratio
Lateral Tire Forces
The Slip Angle
Combining the longitudinal and lateral components
The Friction Circle
From a driver's point of view
Integration onto the chassis
Cars are everywhere in games. They're a staple element of many genres, even in games that aren't strictly about cars. If a game world involves any sort of traversal, chances are there's a vehicle in it (unless you're deep in the realm of fantasy where you are riding a horse. The following will not cover programming horses, I apologize).
The special case of cars
The range of experiences that games offer through vehicles is massive. And that's what makes them fascinating to work with. Ever since I was a kid, I've played a variety of racing and vehicle games. I'd always chase the next racing title as soon as it hit the platform I had. But what struck me over time wasn't just the excitement of new cars or tracks; it was how different each experience felt, even though they all had cars at their core.
And here's the key insight: games are not physics engines. They are experiences. And racing games, more than many others, deliberately manipulate reality to deliver those experiences. With shooting games, for example, we expect certain behavior; bullets flying in straight lines, recoil, reloads. If those expectations aren't met, the game feels “off.” But with vehicles? There's an incredible amount of wiggle room.
Take Mario Kart. It's about as far from realistic driving as you can get; you're drifting on sand, tossing shells at your friends, and racing in a mushroom-powered go-kart that's all squashed proportions and cartoon physics. And yet it's beloved. It sells the fantasy of driving.
On the opposite end, you have full-blown simulators like iRacing or Assetto Corsa. Here, the experience is carefully crafted to reflect the nuance and challenge of real-life motorsport. People sink thousands of dollars into rigs just to replicate the feeling of being behind the wheel. And yet; both these games are programming cars at their core. They just prioritize different aspects of that experience.
So why the variability? Why can games get away with such a broad spectrum of driving models?
It's because when it comes to cars, we derive our expectations of them not just from first hand experience. Our understanding of what “driving fast” feels like is often built from second-hand sources; films, games, pop culture. We've all seen the hero of a movie shift gears a dozen times in a straight-line drag race. It's absurd, has nothing to do with reality, but it communicates something. It sells the feeling of acceleration, intensity, control. So kids get it; they want to “shift up” because it feels like doing something meaningful. It's the visceral feeling of controling something large and heavy at break-neck speeds.
So the key question for anyone implementing vehicles in a game isn't “what are the real physics I need to simulate?”, it's “what experience do I want to convey?”. From there you get to the question of “how do I implement that?”.
I've come to realize that the challenge of simulating vehicles in games lies in bridging two complex worlds: the experience and the machine. You need to understand both. Only then can you decide how and where to bend the rules; because game design isn't about simulating reality, it's about shaping it to fit your vision.
Chasing the Feel: The Iterative Path to AV-Racer
My first attempt at simulating a vehicle in a game was AV Racer, and it began as a simple top-down sprite using a basic Newtonian model. I controlled the car's movement with acceleration and braking, tied angular velocity to speed (so it wouldn't rotate on the spot), and called it a day.
Did it look like a car? Sort of. Did it feel like one? Not at all. It was more like a robotic puck skating around on invisible rails. So, iterating on that, I started hacking in some nonlinear curves and smoothing functions to mimic a behavior of a sliding car, trying to push away from the rigid feel. I faked the trail, exaggerated the drift, tweaked the angular momentum. It was all hacks, but it worked, somewhat. At least until Casey Muratori tried it and pointed out it looked like a car on ice, a spaceship. And he was right. It floated rather than gripped.
So I went back to the drawing board, already sunk in the hacky method, I added more magical numbers, created a para

• **[furyofantares]** 对文章开头的观点提出质疑，认为游戏中的枪械也有很多不现实的体验，并举例说明多种不同类型的枪械效果。此外，对文章中关于驾驶体验期望的理论缺乏证据支持表示不满。

• **[Animats]** 指出文章中未提及的重要车辆物理元素，如山丘、弯道和悬挂系统，并提到Unreal Engine中的车辆 demo项目，其中一个项目有简单的悬挂模型。

• **[acc_297]** 推荐了一个关于赛车物理的讲座视频，由Andre Marziali讲解，提供了更多关于赛车物理的深入内容。

• **[guhcampos]** 对文章中的错别字进行了纠正，同时表达了对轮胎模拟和发动机声音生成原理的兴趣。

• **[jimmySixDOF]** 提到了一组用于车辆的glTF扩展标准，可以有效地在不同游戏引擎中渲染车辆并协调物理效果。

• **[andrewmcwatters]** 回忆了Halo 1中的车辆物理，尽管其物理机制看似不合理，但驾驶感受非常独特和有趣，并将其与Grand Theft Auto 4中的车辆物理进行了比较。

• **[constantcrying]** 认为文章更多是从游戏开发者角度出发，而非工程师的角度，并提到如果真正想模拟车辆，其实有大量文献可以参考。他还特别提到了BeamNG的模拟方法与传统方法的差异。

• **[matheusmoreira]** 对转向模型的编程表示兴趣，认为转向感觉不佳会严重影响游戏体验，并提到Cyberpunk 2077中的车辆驾驶感非常真实。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于文章开头对车辆和枪械在游戏中不现实体验的比较，[furyofantares]认为枪械同样具有广泛的非现实体验。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于模拟的真实性与游戏趣味性之间的平衡，多个评论者提到了这一点并分享了不同的经验和看法。
• 具体车辆物理元素如轮胎模型、悬挂系统和反摇杆对驾驶体验的影响被多次提及，显示出这些元素在车辆模拟中的重要性。

README.md
dwl - dwm for Wayland
Join us on our IRC channel:
#dwl on Libera Chat
Or on the community-maintained
Discord server
.
dwl is a compact, hackable compositor for
Wayland
based on
wlroots
. It is
intended to fill the same space in the Wayland world that dwm does in X11,
primarily in terms of functionality, and secondarily in terms of
philosophy. Like dwm, dwl is:
Easy to understand, hack on, and extend with patches
One C source file (or a very small number) configurable via
config.h
Tied to as few external dependencies as possible
Getting Started:
Latest semi-stable
release
This is probably where you want to start. This builds against the
wlroots
versions currently shipping in major distributions. If your
distribution's
wlroots
version is older, use an earlier dwl
release
.
The
wlroots
version against which a given
dwl
release builds is specified
with each release on the
release
page
Development branch
main
Active development progresses on the
main
branch. The
main
branch is built
against a late (and often changing) git commit of wlroots. While the adventurous
are welcome to use
main
, it is a rocky road. Using
main
requires that the
user be willing to chase git commits of wlroots. Testing development pull
requests may involve merging unmerged pull requests in
wlroots
' git repository
and/or git commits of wayland.
Building dwl
dwl has the following dependencies:
libinput
wayland
wlroots (compiled with the libinput backend)
xkbcommon
wayland-protocols (compile-time only)
pkg-config (compile-time only)
dwl has the following additional dependencies if XWayland support is enabled:
libxcb
libxcb-wm
wlroots (compiled with X11 support)
Xwayland (runtime only)
Install these (and their
-devel
versions if your distro has separate
development packages) and run
make
. If you wish to build against a released
version of wlroots (
you probably do
), use a
release
or a
0.x branch
. If
you want to use the unstable development
main
branch, you need to use the git
version of
wlroots
.
To enable XWayland, you should uncomment its flags in
config.mk
.
Configuration
All configuration is done by editing
config.h
and recompiling, in the same
manner as dwm. There is no way to separately restart the window manager in
Wayland without restarting the entire display server, so any changes will take
effect the next time dwl is executed.
As in the dwm community, we encourage users to share patches they have
created. Check out the
dwl-patches
repository!
Running dwl
dwl can be run on any of the backends supported by wlroots. This means you can
run it as a separate window inside either an X11 or Wayland session, as well as
directly from a VT console. Depending on your distro's setup, you may need to
add your user to the
video
and
input
groups before you can run dwl on a
VT. If you are using
elogind
or
systemd-logind
you need to install polkit;
otherwise you need to add yourself in the
seat
group and enable/start the
seatd daemon.
When dwl is run with no arguments, it will launch the server and begin handling
any shortcuts configured in
config.h
. There is no status bar or other

data.title: It's DE9, Not DB9
data.author: jgrahamc
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了D-sub连接器的命名误用，特别指出常见的9针串行端口通常被称为DB9，而实际上正确的技术名称为DE9。文章解释了D-sub系列连接器的命名规则，其中第二个字母代表外壳尺寸，"E"对应9针外壳，而"B"对应25针外壳。尽管DB9这一错误名称广泛流传并成为默认标准，SparkFun在其新推出的DE9连接器分线板中坚持使用正确的名称，以推广技术准确性并教育社区。文章呼吁在使用技术术语时应追求准确性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于技术连接器名称准确性及使用习惯的讨论

不同观点：
• [HocusLocus] 认为，20世纪80年代时，由于某些插图未被广泛展示，插图师因此出错，导致现在名称上的混乱。他强调任意字母和描述性数字组合是问题的根源，但总体上对人们在标准改进中的表现持积极态度。
• [dlcarrier] 指出，8P8C和RJ45是不同的术语，8P8C是标准术语，而RJ45更为大众所知。他建议在文档中使用准确的术语，但也应注明常见的俗称。
• [zettabomb] 对D-sub连接器的长寿表示赞赏，尽管个人不会首选这种连接器，但承认其在多个领域的持久应用。
• [9rx] 质疑DB9这一名称的不准确性，认为DB壳体可以容纳9针连接器，尽管实际上没有这样的产品。
• [brudgers] 认为人们并没有误用D-sub连接器的术语，因为大家在不同的语境下使用这些术语，并且彼此理解。
• [alnwlsn] 提到其他类似情况，如“复合视频”有多个不同但常被混用的术语，指出技术领域中术语混用的普遍性。
• [dec0dedab0de] 表示自己因为记不住DB9而直接称其为串行端口，并希望记住这些细节能在未来给他带来一些“炫耀”资本。
• [cwillu] 坚持使用DB9，认为这个名称更容易发音且被普遍理解，主张标准应考虑人的习惯和弱点。
• [shermantanktop] 认为技术上的吹毛求疵虽然有趣，但最重要的是语言的沟通功能，过于纠结细节会使对话变得乏味。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术术语的准确性与实际使用中的便利性之间的平衡。一些人主张严格遵守标准术语，而另一些人则认为俗称和习惯用法更具实际意义。
• 讨论中还涉及了其他类似例子，如“复合视频”和“VGA端口”等术语的多重使用和误用现象。
• 一些参与者对技术术语的历史演变表现出兴趣，如D-sub连接器的命名规则及其在不同行业的应用。

It's a DE9, Not a DB9. (But We Know What You Mean)
by
Christo-boots with the-pher
July 21, 2025
Engineering
History
You have been misusing the D-sub connector terminology, and we're guilty of it, too.
You’ve seen them everywhere, especially on older computer equipment: the classic 9-pin serial connector. You probably know it as a DB9. It’s an iconic connector for makers, engineers, and anyone who's ever used an RS232 serial device. Here's a little secret, though: calling it a DB9 is technically wrong. The correct name is actually DE9.
With the release of our new DE9 Connector Breakouts, we wanted to address a common misconception and explain why we named our boards as we did.
SparkFun DE9 Breakout - Male
BOB-29195
Easily connect with the SparkFun DE9 Male Breakout, a compact board that brings all nine DE9 pins to a convenient 0.1in. spac…
$3.95
SparkFun DE9 Breakout - Female
BOB-29196
Easily connect with the SparkFun DE9 Female Breakout, a compact board that brings all nine DE9 pins to a convenient 0.1in. sp…
$3.95
In the Interest of Fairness:
We are omitting the "-" in "DE-9" and "DB-25." We have found that using a "-" is optional in writing this information.
What's in a Name? The D-Subminiature Standard
The connector in question belongs to a family known as D-subminiature, or D-sub for short. To put it simply, the "D" in the name comes from the D-shaped metal shield surrounding the pins, which ensures the plug can only be inserted one way!
The full part number for these connectors follows a specific pattern. The first letter is always D for the D-shape. The second letter, however, is where the confusion starts. It doesn't stand for a feature; it specifies the size of the connector's shell. The number that follows indicates the number of pins in that shell.
Here’s a quick breakdown of the standard D-sub shell sizes:
DA
: 15-pin shell
DB
: 25-pin shell (This is the big one you'd see on old parallel printer ports)
DC
: 37-pin shell
DD
: 50-pin shell
DE
: 9-pin shell (Today's topic)
The correct technical designation for a D-sub connector with nine pins is DE9. Although "DB9" is a widely used term, it is a misnomer based on the D-sub naming convention, where the second letter signifies the shell size. The "E" in DE9 denotes the specific shell size that houses nine pins while the letter "B" refers to a larger shell designed for 25 pins, as seen in a correctly named DB25 connector. To be blunt, the term "DB9" is plainly inaccurate because it pairs the 25-pin "B" shell with a 9-pin count, a physical contradiction. Despite this, "DB9" became the de facto standard name and is commonly understood to refer to the 9-pin serial connector.
So, Why Do We All Call It DB9?
The mix-up is a classic case of mistaken identity that just stuck. The original IBM PC used a DB25 connector for its serial and parallel ports. When the smaller 9-pin serial port was introduced on the IBM PC/AT, it quickly became the new standard for serial ports.
Most people, already familiar with the term "DB25," simply swapped the number of pins and started calling the new connector a DB9. The incorrect name spread like wildfire and became the de facto standard term, despite being technically inaccurate. It's a prime example of typical usage winning out over technical accuracy.
Our Naming Philosophy: Correctness and Clarity
With the launch of our new
SparkFun Male DE9 Breakout
and
SparkFun Female DE9 Breakout
, we made a conscious decision to use the technically correct name. This blog post is our explanation for why.
At SparkFun, we are engineers, makers, and educators at heart. We believe in technical accuracy and in sharing our knowledge with the community. While we know that a vast majority of people search for "DB9," we felt it was essential to stick to the correct DE9 designation for our products.
It’s our small way of doing our part to correct a decades-old mix-up. We want our product names to be accurate and serve as a learning opportunity for anyone curious about the "why." So when you see the "DE9" on our new breakouts, you'll know that the name is as intentional as the engineering that went into the board itself.
So, while the world might continue to refer to it as DB9, we'll call it for what it is: a DE9. Happy hacking!

• [zettabomb] 对D-sub连接器的长寿表示赞赏，尽管个人不会首选这种连接器，但承认其在多个领域的持久应用。
• [9rx] 质疑DB9这一名称的不准确性，认为DB壳体可以容纳9针连接器，尽管实际上没有这样的产品。
• [brudgers] 认为人们并没有误用D-sub连接器的术语，因为大家在不同的语境下使用这些术语，并且彼此理解。
• [alnwlsn] 提到其他类似情况，如“复合视频”有多个不同但常被混用的术语，指出技术领域中术语混用的普遍性。
• [dec0dedab0de] 表示自己因为记不住DB9而直接称其为串行端口，并希望记住这些细节能在未来给他带来一些“炫耀”资本。
• [cwillu] 坚持使用DB9，认为这个名称更容易发音且被普遍理解，主张标准应考虑人的习惯和弱点。
• [shermantanktop] 认为技术上的吹毛求疵虽然有趣，但最重要的是语言的沟通功能，过于纠结细节会使对话变得乏味。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术术语的准确性与实际使用中的便利性之间的平衡。一些人主张严格遵守标准术语，而另一些人则认为俗称和习惯用法更具实际意义。
• 讨论中还涉及了其他类似例子，如“复合视频”和“VGA端口”等术语的多重使用和误用现象。
• 一些参与者对技术术语的历史演变表现出兴趣，如D-sub连接器的命名规则及其在不同行业的应用。

data.title: Show HN: The Montana MiniComputer
data.author: recursivedoubts
data.article_summary: Montana Mini-Computer (MTMC-16)是一台16位虚拟计算机，旨在以有趣且直观的方式展示数字计算原理。它结合了PDP-11、MIPS、Scott CPU、Game Boy和JVM的设计理念，具备基本的计算能力。用户通过网页界面操作，界面包含控制台、显示器、计算机状态的可视化表示以及内置代码编辑器。MTMC-16拥有4KB内存、16个寄存器和160x144像素的2-bit绿阶显示屏。它运行MTOS操作系统，支持文本输入/输出和命令控制台。使用MTMC-16需要Java 21及以上版本的虚拟机和现代网页浏览器。项目文档和安装指南可从其官网和GitHub页面获取。

The Montana Mini-Computer / MTMC-16 Homepage
The MonTana state Mini Computer is a virtual computer intended to show how digital computation works in a fun and visual way.
The MTSC combines ideas from the PDP-11, MIPS, Scott CPU, Game Boy and JVM to make a relatively simple 16-bit computer that can accomplish basic computing tasks.
The computer is displayed via a web interface that includes all the I/O such as console and display, visual representations of the computer state, and a built in code editor to construct and debug software for the computer.

data.title: Who has the fastest F1 website (2021)
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文是关于2021年F1车队网站加载速度的系列评测之三，主要分析Red Bull车队官网的性能。相比2019年，2021年的Red Bull网站显著提速，总加载时间从15.8秒减少到8.6秒。然而，仍存在一些可优化的问题，如由于不必要的内嵌代码导致内容渲染延迟3秒，主图像由于JavaScript实现和优化不足延迟10秒以上，此外还有字体和关键图像的加载延迟。通过优化图像格式（如使用更小体积的AVIF）、精简内嵌代码和改善资源加载策略，网站性能还有进一步提升空间。总体而言，Red Bull网站虽视觉丰富，但仍有改进潜力。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• GaggiX：详细讨论了WebP格式在色彩表现上的缺陷，指出其无法关闭子采样，并推荐使用AVIF格式，认为AVIF得到了所有主流浏览器的支持，是更好的选择。此评论提供了技术细节和替代方案。

• 实际应用：讨论中涉及到多个实际案例和项目链接（如snug的F1网站），但多数未深入展开技术细节。
• 历史反馈：hhmc提出的关于反馈落实的问题，显示出对实际应用效果的关注。

整体来看，讨论围绕图片格式选择、格式特性及其实际应用展开，不同参与者提供了各自的见解和经验。

44682932.article_content:
Who has the fastest F1 website in 2021? Part 3
Posted 29 March 2021
I once spent an hour creating an
F1 lights-out reaction test
which went viral and was even
played by F1 drivers
. That sounds like a brag, and it kinda is, but now whenever I pour days or even weeks of work into something, it just seems so inefficient compared to that time I spent
an hour
on something that went big. Wait! You're not my therapist! Let's look at another F1 website…
This is part 3 in a multi-part series looking at the loading performance of F1 websites. Not interested in F1? It shouldn't matter. This is just a performance review of 10 recently-built/updated sites that have broadly the same goal, but are built by different teams, and have different performance issues.
Part 1: Methodology & Alpha Tauri
Part 2: Alfa Romeo
➡️ Part 3: Red Bull
Part 4: Williams
Part 5: Aston Martin
Part 6: Ferrari
Part 7: Haas
Part 8: McLaren
Bonus: Google I/O
…more coming soon…
Red Bull
Link
Red Bull Racing Honda
First run
6.7s (
raw results
)
Second run
1.9s (
raw results
)
Total
8.6s
2019 total
15.8s (2021 site is 7.2s faster)
Now we're talking! This is a graphically rich, engaging site, and the performance is pretty good! In fact, it's significantly faster than its 2019 site. But there's still room for improvement.
Possible improvements
3 second delay to content-render
caused by unnecessary inlining. Covered in detail below.
10 second delay to main image
caused by a JavaScript responsive images implementation,
like we saw in part 2
. These should be
real responsive images
.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by an extra connection. This problem is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the images to the same server as the page.
Additional 2 second delay to main image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
40 second delay to key image
caused by loading it with JavaScript. Covered in detail below.
Additional 30 second delay to that image
caused by poor optimisation. Covered in detail below.
2 second delay to fonts
caused by extra connection. Again, this is
covered in part 1
, but the solution here is just to move the fonts to the same server.
40+ second delay to content-blocking cookie modal
caused by… a number of things,
covered in part 1
.
Remember these delays overlap in some cases.
Issue: Unnecessary inlining
Here's the first bit of the timeline:
The page renders around the 6s mark, which is while the HTML is still downloading. Browsers can stream HTML and render it while it's downloading; it's a great feature of parsed-HTML that many sites don't get the benefit of due to blocking resources. Because the page renders with that one resource, we know there are
no
blocking resources. This suggests the CSS is inlined, and from looking at the source, yep, it is.
Inlining avoids request/response overhead, which is great for render-blocking resources. But also, since it's part of the
page
, you can tailor the inlining for
that page
.
However, that doesn't seem to be what's happening here. Here's what I see in
Chrome DevTools' coverage panel
:
The code in the page is 79.5% unused, which amounts to over 600kB. Compare this to the coverage on
Squoosh
:
…where we used inline content just for the CSS and script needed for the first interaction. The first row there is a non-blocking resource, where coverage doesn't matter so much, but the bottom row is the page, where only 7kB is unused. You can also click on these lines which takes you to a code view of used and unused code:
Anyway, we aren't here to talk about Squoosh. Around three seconds could be shaved off time-to-content on the Red Bull site by making the inlined code tailored to what the page needs for that content-render. The rest can be loaded via external resources.
Issue: Large primary image
Original WebP (99.1 kB)
Optimised WebP (24.8 kB)
AVIF (13.9 kB)
It's great to see them using WebP, but the quality is just set too high. Yes, some detail is lost in the compressed versions, but remember this image has text over the top, and another image over the top.
Actually, let's talk about that image…
Issue: Large overlay image
Original WebP (1.1 MB)
Optimised WebP (620 kB)
AVIF (132 kB)
AVIF for mobile (47.8 kB)
This image sits over the top of the main carousel, and it's a great part of the design. Again, they're using WebP, but maybe not with the right settings. But even with optimised settings, the WebP is still big.
When WebP was created, they designed the alpha channel around things like logos, and things cut-out of photos. In these cases the alpha channel is dominated by large areas of the same value:
Full image
Alpha channel
Because of this, they used the WebP
lossless
mode for the alpha channel, even if the colour data is using the lossy mode. This works well in general, except in cases like this:
Full image
Alpha channel
…where the alpha channel is frequently changing. This is something a lossy codec handles much better. AVIF can perform lossy encodi

• 历史反馈：hhmc提出的关于反馈落实的问题，显示出对实际应用效果的关注。

整体来看，讨论围绕图片格式选择、格式特性及其实际应用展开，不同参与者提供了各自的见解和经验。

data.title: Up to date prices for LLM APIs all in one place
data.author: alexellman
data.article_summary: 该文章提供了截至2025年7月25日的各大语言模型API（如OpenAI、Anthropic、Google等）的最新价格信息，帮助用户比较不同模型的成本，找到最具性价比的选择。文章列出了26个模型的输入和输出成本，以每百万 tokens 为单位，并注明部分模型根据提示长度采用分层定价。文章还提供了价格图表和订阅更新服务，由@aellman创建，并提供每周更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的版本和价格信息的管理与比较

不同观点：
• binarymax：希望找到一个API来维护和获取所有模型版本及其价格信息，目前依赖手动更新OpenAI的价格信息并保存在JSON文件中，用于成本报告和npm包llm-primitives中。
• alexellman：提到LLM提供商不断更新模型和价格，推荐自己创建的pricepertoken.com网站，汇总了最新模型的价格，并计划加入图像模型的价格比较。
• mythz：指出pricepertoken.com上的数据有误，例如Google Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite的成本被错误显示。
• awongh：认为仅提供价格信息不足，还需考虑不同提供商对相同模型的不同定价、速度和成本优化、量化版本、批量定价等复杂因素，并提到artificialanalysis.ai提供的混合成本模型有助于排序。
• criddell：关注在本地运行模型的硬件预算问题，询问在2500美元预算下的可行性及相关教程推荐。
• CharlesW：提到Simon Willison的LLM定价计算器作为参考资源。
• pierre：指出不同提供商和模型之间的token不等价问题，例如GPT-4o-mini和Gemini 2.5 pro的token计算差异。
• callbacked：建议将OpenRouter加入价格比较，但指出其网站布局不便于数据抓取。
• lucasoshiro：赞赏UI界面简洁，但指出缺少如Gemma、DeepSeek等更多模型。
• alienbaby：希望比较价格以决定使用如Copilot Pro或Claude等服务的更经济方案。
• kb_geek：建议加入模型的性能排名和基准测试信息以帮助理解模型的能力。
• uponasmile：赞赏UX设计，认为界面干净直观，色彩使用清晰。
• dgrin91：建议加入时间维度以追踪价格变化。
• jalopy：关注如何通过实验和工具使用便宜模型达到昂贵模型的性能，例如通过CoT（Chain of Thought）方法提升Gemini 2.5 flash的输出质量。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：pricepertoken.com上的数据准确性受到mythz的质疑，指出Google Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite的成本显示错误。
• 其他重要讨论点：不同模型之间的token不等价问题、提供商对相同模型的不同定价策略、以及在本地运行模型的硬件预算和可行性。

data.title: Meta to stop running political ads on Facebook and Instagram in the EU
data.author: aquir
data.article_summary: Meta宣布将从10月起停止在欧盟投放政治、选举和社会议题广告，以避免遵守即将生效的欧盟透明度法规。该法规要求披露政治广告的资金来源及是否使用个人数据进行定向投放，旨在防止信息操纵和外国干涉选举。Meta称这些新规对广告商和平台造成了过度的复杂性和法律不确定性。此前，谷歌也做出了类似决定。欧盟议员Sandro Gozi批评Meta此举是对透明度和民主责任的逃避，质疑其打击虚假信息的承诺。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta停止政治广告在欧盟的影响及相关问题

不同观点：
• [poisonborz] 指出匈牙利政府是欧盟内Meta政治广告的最大支出者，担忧其影响，特别是与德国或欧盟议会相比的显著支出。
• [ajdude] 认为即使屏蔽了政治广告，Facebook上仍有许多非广告的政治内容通过病毒式传播，屏蔽功能效果有限。
• [isodev] 支持政治广告不该存在，认为这是好消息。
• [CommenterPerson] 赞同此举，认为欧盟正在通过一些好的法规来应对互联网的恶化问题。
• [game_the0ry] 感叹社交网络对当今世界的影响，从其创始人的背景联想到当前局势。
• [blitzar] 认为Meta停止政治广告没有损失任何有价值的东西，甚至其股价也未受影响。
• [seydor] 指出欧盟委员会和议会本身就是Facebook上最大的广告商之一，质疑这些是否算作政治广告。
• [Yoric] 简单表达对此消息的积极态度，认为是最好的消息。
• [jabjq] 认为最成功的政治广告通常不是付费的，而是通过其他方式传播的。
• [progbits] 讽刺Meta律师因监管和政治广告透明度规则而需要额外工作，暗示这些规则的必要性。
• [sam-cop-vimes] 简单表达对Meta停止政治广告的支持，认为是清除糟粕。
• [yostrovs] 提出所有涉及意见或试图改变他人想法的言论都应该透明化，以便听众了解背后的意图。
• [mrtksn] 详细描述了政治广告如何被用于操纵舆论，包括右翼和左翼的例子，以及外国干预选举的问题，认为停止政治广告有助于减少这种操纵。
• [duxup] 提出具体情境，质疑如果候选人因特定政策（如“禁止池塘中的鸭子”）而出名，是否可以通过广告来强化此议题，以影响选民。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于政治广告是否应该存在，以及其对政治舆论和选举的潜在影响。
• 讨论中也提到了非付费政治内容通过社交媒体传播的问题，这可能削弱仅限制政治广告的效果。
• 外国干预和政治宣传的透明度问题也被提及，强调了更广泛的监管需求。
• 最后，一些评论对Meta停止政治广告的实际影响持怀疑态度，认为可能不会带来实质性的改变或损失。

The social media giant blames an upcoming EU regulation that would require it to comply with political ads transparency rules.

Updates
Updated to include a response statement from the regulation's rapporteur.
Social media giant Meta announced today that it will stop running political, electoral or social issue advertising in the EU from October, instead of complying with the bloc's transparency rules for political advertising.
EU-wide rules on the transparency of political advertising come into effect from October, with the aim of curbing information manipulation and foreign interference during elections, according to a Council
announcement
on the agreement last year.
The regulation obliges online publishers of political advertisements to disclose whether an ad is paid for by a political actor to make it easier for citizens to recognise political marketing. It also requires disclosure of whether the ad was targeted using personal data.
Meta is sidestepping all these requirements, per its announcement today, as the company says it will no longer allow political, electoral or social issue ads in the EU. It defines these types of ads in its terms and conditions for different territories. Meta said the change would also apply in other "European territories", including the UK.
The company is blaming its decision to end political ads on the EU's Regulation – claiming it's too restrictive and burdensome for advertisers. "Unfortunately, the TTPA [the political ads transparency regulation] introduces significant additional obligations to our processes and systems that create an untenable level of complexity and legal uncertainty for advertisers and platforms operating in the EU," Meta
wrote
.
It said the move won't change any of its other policies for people in the EU as regards debating politics. Nor will it stop politicians from posting content on its social networks. However political actors would not be able to pay Meta to amplify such content.
Responding to Meta's announcement, liberal lawmaker Sandro Gozi, the rapporteur for the EU's regulation on political advertising, said it "confirms a deep allergy to transparency, data protection and democratic accountability." "They [Meta] pretend to fight disinformation, but in reality they are making money from it," he added.
Last year, Google also
announced
that it would stop serving political ads in the EU before the regulation came into effect. It blamed the law for having an overly broad definition of "political advertisement" for it to be able to comply, hence choosing to stop running such ads across the bloc.
But one question both companies' actions raises is how effective their own – typically automated – ad review systems are at detecting political, electoral or social issue ads and stopping them from being distributed. Any political ads that do slip through would automatically breach the EU's transparency rules given their ad systems do not provide these disclosures.
In Meta's case, this is not the first time it's blamed EU laws for forcing it to change its ad behaviour: the tech giant is currently
facing
Digital Markets Act enforcement over its pay-or-consent advertising model.
